synthesis.north_star: Butlers is a superset of Dots for one owner: everything Dots does for a person (research, finished files, mail, monitoring, long projects) Butlers does with more reach (the house, the phone, money, health, place) and stronger guarantees: the owner sees the exact call before it runs, every live link says where it came from, nothing spends, nothing reaches another person without the owner, and the fleet never outspends the owner's ceiling.

ranked_moves.title: Cost governance across the RFC 0038 switch: a fail-closed monthly fleet pool with an owner reserve, plus origin-aware starting rungs
ranked_moves.why: Today's monthly ceiling lives only in the spawner (spawner.py:2172-2215; check_monthly_ceiling in model_routing.py ~3080), fails open, and halts owner turns too. RFC 0038 deletes the spawner and names no successor, which three lenses found independently, so after the switch spend is bounded only per goal. Dispatch intent derives from role only, so inbound chatter runs on the same rung as the owner's own turns.
ranked_moves.payoff: With a $100 ceiling, background stops at $80 and the owner keeps $20 (about 250 owner goals at $0.079); /status shows 'obligation lane 78% of $40, owner reserve intact'. A small first rung for third-party leads saves about 65% (about $61 a month at 40 goals a day; breakeven escalation rate 94%).
ranked_moves.outcome: After the switch the owner's monthly model ceiling still holds, now fail-closed: goal admission reserves against a fleet month pool split into origin lanes (owner, obligation, third_party, staffer), background lanes stop at (1-r) of the ceiling so owner goals keep a reserve (default 20%), a ledger or lane read error refuses background work and gives owner goals a templated reply, the owner gets one templated Telegram notice at 80% and at the ceiling (no model call), and third-party and obligation leads start on the small rung while owner leads carry a latency deadline.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No transact or payments. No change to per-goal D10 budgets or the research host's own daily cap. No model can raise a cap: cap changes are owner-only administer effects. No edits to the frozen spawner beyond what bu-svqpzo.3 already owns.

Failure: an unreadable ledger or lane refuses background admissions and gives owner goals a deterministic 'spend state unreadable' reply. Concurrency: lane decrements happen in the same D7 transaction as goal budgets, so racing goals cannot overshoot by more than one reservation. Idempotence: the reservation is keyed by goal_id, and a recovery epoch reuses it. Rollback: set the lanes flag off and fall back to the per-goal budgets alone. Tier unavailable: an exhausted allowance defers obligation goals; an owner goal falls through to the next account per excluded_allowance.
Assurance: Owner reserve guarantee: survives in the admission transaction, not in model behavior (D16: model choice is never security). Fail-closed D10: survives because lane reads share the budget transaction. No new reach: lanes only refuse or defer work and never grant capability. Prompt injection: third-party content cannot raise a cap, because cap changes are administer effects that are park-only and approved per event. Add the reversible bulk-actuation hole. switch/light/fan turn_off with an area, device or 'all' target, or on a critical plug, is ungated even under exposure (actuation.py:23-33,84-93; security.md:84-87). This is a Dots-study-class reach hole that no child covers.

Say explicitly that citations are model claims (bu-6qaju2.3 output contract line 9) and can never become a live link. Only urls_opened may (pursuit run 19 deep-design-1).

Part 5 should separate caller-supplied buttons from server-built typed actions. Caller url buttons should be refused, and login_url and web_app refused always, because they send the owner's signed Telegram identity to the site. Server-built open_link and open_dashboard actions resolved from link references stay live under render_links_inert. Otherwise exposed approval and decision cards lose their Open button. telegram_api.py:43-86 is the place to change.

The exact-call card gate should also require binding the presented args digest: approval_delivery_presentations.args_digest, checked at callback time. Today's token binds only action_id:verb:requested_at (core/approval_callbacks.py:78-82).

Its per-tool preview registry should be the approval card's single registry. A preview truncated at 1,500 characters must suppress Approve and Reject (Open only) and must not present a truncated view as approvable. Body URLs render inert on the card.

The bead's design already names the run 19 move; make it name the link-reference resolver too, so the provenance columns are read at migration time.

Item (d) 'approvals with lineage' should serve one approval-lineage read model, used by both the dashboard page and the Telegram exact-call card (S2), so phone and dashboard show identical facts. Goal-page source links should render through the shared link-reference resolver.
The exact-call card needs content_params as well as recipient_params, to know which arguments to show as content. Without them it falls back to showing every non-recipient argument, or Open only.

Its dashboard route register should also exist on the server (route_key to path pattern with typed params), as the allowlist for self link references. That lets every Telegram dashboard link be validated as well as tested for phone use.

Under-prioritised (P3, blocked). Haiku 5.5 (5x above 100K) and GPT-6 Luna are the named monitor and child candidates (bu-juscql), and D10 spend budgets fail closed on metered spend, so upper-tier turns would be undercounted up to 5x. Price per request turn from the runtime usage stream, not per session aggregate, and make it a prerequisite of bu-u5s4w8's spend metering.

Budgets are per goal only. There is no fleet monthly ceiling successor (spawner.py:2172-2215 dies at the switch; the catalog-token-limits delta line 53 makes only the per-model quota fail closed). Add a lane or ceiling check in the D7 transaction or depend on the spend-lanes move.

Obligation conversion drops the scheduler's allowance deferral (docs/runtime/model-routing.md:332-336: skipped_allowance moving next_run_at to reset). Name its goal-admission successor. The declaration format should also reserve a precondition field (move 3).

Targets the frozen spawner (dispatch_governance and lane caps). Re-scope to goal-runtime lanes keyed by origin, obligation id or staffer contract, or supersede by the spend-lanes move. Its 84.9% QA-lane evidence remains the key justification.
The P4 'background reserve for owner turns' is on the frozen path and allowance-only. Supersede by an owner reserve in goal-runtime spend lanes that covers both USD and allowance deferral.
The replay should output per-origin starting rungs and an owner-turn deadline (not only per-role tiers), report escalation rate per origin, and price with context tiers (depends on bu-fphibb).

Reserve goals.project_ref (nullable, server-held only) and budget_pools/pool_reservations in the first ledger migration. Pools cover the fleet monthly ceiling, project envelopes and the 'admission budget for high-volume feeds' this bead must settle anyway. Settle replies to completed senders: admit an owner-origin goal (not caused) with project_ref, and carry a delivery reference rather than the quoted card text.

Caps concurrency only. The owner's monthly spend ceiling (public.spend_ceiling, checked fail-open at spawner.py:2182) has no successor after the switch. File a sibling bead or extend scope for a fail-closed fleet_month budget pool at admission.

Runtime-created obligations should carry bundle_id and project_id plus until_at so that one approved administer call can arm, and one disarm can cancel, a set of rows. Project check-ins must be continuity=false, since a tainted carry_forward starts every occurrence exposed (core-scheduler delta :155).

For a Telegram reply to the bot's own message, carry reply_to message_id as a server-resolvable reference and do not mark the bot's text as a quoted third-party span. Otherwise every owner reply to a card starts exposed under D5:398.

Reserve a projects strip on the overview (armed projects, next wake, decisions waiting, pool use) and a 'projects drawing on this region' list on region pages. The slice 1 project page should be adopted into this change.
/status should also list armed projects with next wake and envelope use, read from ledger and General rows only. /hold should disarm or skip project occurrences without cancelling their bundles.

Document the research-first pattern (charter-only children delegated before any stamped read, one live call each) in lead guidance via bu-kfnoah. Add a suite case showing that a probe issued after a project_log read runs cached.

Its 'knowledge-classed profile pack' (Profile Facts) is assembled into per-butler memory_context by the frozen spawner (spawner.py:2380 fetch_memory_context). After the switch, memory reaches leads only through context.search, and the system prompt carries the RFC 0038 'owner profile' (core-spawner delta spec.md:249). Re-scope the profile-pack part to feed the D15 owner profile, or mark it frozen-path, so the work is not stranded.

No bead asks the owner the WhatsApp send ban-risk question (roster/messenger/butler.toml:63-66 send_enabled=false; study gap_matrix_reach_actions.md:53 Q2). J15 and D3 stay open by default. File an owner HOLD or record WhatsApp send as an owner exclusion.

Run 19's 'one approval arms a project's whole check-in plan' (lens-long-goals) is the same owner-signed, time-boxed grant-bundle substrate. Shape Absence Plans as the generic bundle that both use, so two arming mechanisms are not built.

Under-scoped. It specifies a trusted editor only for the Chronicler SSID-place mapping, but the same concept lives in env OWNTRACKS_PLACE_REFERENCES (context_producers.py:641, owntracks_place_cluster.py:162) and in the home:presence:owner_entities key (bu-bdlr3). Widen it to one owner_places registry and editor, or three editors will exist for one concept.

Routing all unsolicited notify through the broker would regress time-anchored and life-safety delivery to the hourly urgent sub-cycle (butler.toml:91-95; RFC 0011:332). Add two acceptance conditions: a minute-resolution timed lane must exist before time-anchored producers migrate, and deterministic life-safety producers keep direct priority-high notify plus owner_conditions.

The retention protocol preserves movement summaries, but leave-by needs place-to-place leg durations (place_episode A to place_episode B), which no projection computes today. Add a travel_legs derivation, or a backfill from labelled place_episode sequences, to the 'projection before forgetting' gate so the owner's trip history survives the 30-day purge.

State explicitly that deterministic presence, departure and safety producers are D2 'unchanged' jobs (RFC 0038:221-222) and must not be converted into obligation admissions. A leak alert or departure card must never depend on goal admission, the budget or model availability.
Fold into the owner_places editor (move 1 S1): owner presence entities are one presence source among HA person, OwnTracks GPS, region and SSID, and should be configured on the same owner page.

Budget is metered in D10. Owner-origin default grant; obligation grants opt in. Amend RFC 0038 (D21, and narrow the :115 non-goal), security.md 'Session Sandboxing' and v1.md …

The cross-source monitor (bu-kqme7f.3) leaves out location, transactions and wearables in v1, so the location, money and recovery fusions below build beyond it rather than duplicating it. Two candidates from the brief are already covered: "where did my day go" is the Chronicler's day-close plus its lanes, and destination weather is atmosphere_consumers.run_travel_destination_outlo…

findings.title: The cross-source monitor's v1 read set excludes location, transactions and wearables

findings.title: The broker cannot deliver time-anchored observations on time

The 13:00-14:00 gap is the only open hour.' It stays silent when either signal is within band, with an expected rate of 0-2 a week. Nothing contains it in the meantime, and no dependency edge records that guard as the blocker. The same chain (svqpzo.1 -> .2 -> bu-fg499t…

findings.title: Confirmed live calendar approval bypass is stalled behind a tooling guard with no containment and no dependency edge
findings.evidence: calendar.py:3833,4238,4435,4474,4513,4787,4962,5100 publish _approval_bypass; :4997/:5127 skip the gate on it; :10009/:10474 store it. svqpzo.2 description: introspection on FastMCP 3.4.2 lists it in the input schema of all 8 tools. svqpzo.1 ROOT note 03:56Z: candidate 'source-qualified CLEAN' but 'actual required guard REFUSED generic unproven-test-or-assertion-loss', worktree quarantined. The real blockers bu-bfbatq (blocked) and bu-ihitkl (in_progress) are not dependency edges; .1 depends only on bu-1g5h40 (blocked review).
findings.detail: An injection in email or an invite can make a relationship or messenger session delete or toggle a butler-event series, or rewrite a large series, without approval. svqpzo.1's own design names containment (server-side registration removal) as a separate ROOT decision, and nobody has made it. The chain also gates M4 and the switch: bu-fg499t -> svqpzo.2 -> .1.

findings.title: svqpzo.1 and svqpzo.2 implement the same fix and make opposite decisions
findings.evidence: svqpzo.2 ACs 1-4,7,8 (remove the param, inert bypass, approved replay, digest binding, reminder tests, docs) duplicate the svqpzo.1 adopted packet. svqpzo.2 design: '[decision] chose fail-closed for those legacy rows over a shim'. svqpzo.1 ROOT adoption: legacy marker retired 'only after exact locked stored binding' (a shim). svqpzo.2 AC4 says a changed replay 'parks again'; .1 says a tampered stored dispatch 'refuses before effect and never substitutes'. ROOT note: '.2 ... all eight original obligations retained'.
findings.detail: Whoever picks up .2 after .1 lands faces six already-satisfied ACs and one that contradicts the adopted behavior. Only ACs 5 (series-scope gate) and 6 (overlap replay) are new work.

findings.title: kqme7f.6 lets third-party and exposed goals write Gmail drafts ungated, contradicting owner choice A
findings.evidence: kqme7f.6 design table: 'gmail_save_draft | record | ... | not gated'. Its [decision]: 'allow gmail_save_draft as a record effect ... from exposed and third-party-origin goals'. Owner boundary recorded on bu-4m4e42 (2026-10-14/15 walkthrough): 'drafts from exposed or third-party goals reach the owner only as parked effects with lineage'.
findings.detail: An attacker-steered draft lands in the owner's real Drafts folder with live links (render_links_inert covers only the approval envelope). It has no lineage and can be sent with one tap from the phone Gmail app. The bead reinterprets an owner decision without asking the owner.

findings.title: kqme7f.5 lets inbound-mail goals archive and mark-read the owner's mail without approval
findings.evidence: kqme7f.5 design: gmail_modify_threads 'record ... not gated'. 'Accepted consequence: under exposure and for third-party goals it runs without approval (D4 record row; D5 third-party ceiling)'. Cap 50 threads per call, with no per-goal call cap. AC: 'A third-party-origin invocation's gmail_modify_threads call dispatches without parking'.
findings.detail: A phishing email can make its own third-party goal archive or mark read the bank's or provider's security alerts. That hides evidence in the owner's external inbox. The record class itself is defensible under D4. The defect is putting this effect inside the third-party ceiling.

findings.title: bu-n92tmr fleet cap can deadlock: parents waiting on queued children or research keep their slots
findings.evidence: bu-n92tmr design: 'every origin (owner, obligation or schedule, event, delegation child, research invocations from epic bu-6qaju2) passes through it'; '[decision] chose queue-then-run over reject'. RFC 0038:586 'goal.await | Wait for or poll child results'. bu-6qaju2.4: the broker launches the research invocation while the caller's call is open. No AC covers a waiting holder.
findings.detail: With 5 slots held by leads that are each in goal.await or an in-flight web_research call, their children queue forever. The fleet stalls and owner Stop is the only exit.

findings.title: Calendar high-impact and recurrence gates fail open on the 5 calendar butlers without approvals, and no bead owns it
findings.evidence: calendar.py:10002 'if approval_bypass or self._approval_enqueuer is None: return None'; :10470 'if self._approval_enqueuer is None: return None'. [modules.calendar] without [modules.approvals] in roster/general, health, finance, lifestyle, travel butler.toml. svqpzo.2 non-goal: 'Adding approval gates to butlers that enable calendar without the approvals module ... out of scope'. svqpzo.3 lists only permissions, ceiling, quota and pause.
findings.detail: openspec module-calendar requires large series and following mutations to be approval-gated, and epic bu-svqpzo AC2 says no control may claim an effect it does not enforce. On those 5 butlers, any injected session can rewrite or delete a large recurring series in the owner's calendar. Removing the bypass flag does not close this.

findings.title: bu-6qaju2.4 hard-depends on the owner HOLD bu-6qaju2.2 though only its live dev proof needs the credential
findings.evidence: bu-6qaju2.2 design: 'Closing this bead on the owner's answer releases the dev live-research proof in this epic's broker capability bead'. Default if unanswered: 'the switch cannot ship'. bu-6qaju2.4 deps include bu-6qaju2.2:blocks. Only AC9 ('one live cited answer ... on the dev release candidate') needs it. bu-enbrs2 and bu-fd3le7 both depend on 6qaju2.4.
findings.detail: The broker capability, budgets, lineage and adversarial tests (ACs 1-8) are hermetic. Waiting on the owner's answer delays them and the switch for no technical reason.

findings.title: The owner Gmail track waits on the run-18 owner HOLD through bu-dss7he.7 despite a stated fallback
findings.evidence: bu-kqme7f.5 deps: bu-dss7he.7:blocks. bu-dss7he.7 deps: bu-i4khaz:blocks. bu-i4khaz '[HOLD] Platform simplification pursuit run 18 — release gate' (open). kqme7f.5 design: 'Fallback if bu-dss7he.7 is closed without landing mint_access_token: extract the Gmail connector's exchange'. kqme7f.6 and .7 depend on .5. kqme7f.1 chose 'no dependency edge on bu-dss7he.7'.
findings.detail: Epic AC1 (Gmail in the cutover gate) depends on an unrelated owner release gate, and nothing in the bead set says so.

findings.title: bu-idcqzy amends RFC 0038 D14 with no owner-approval gate, and literal REQ-017 remains in two beads
findings.evidence: bu-idcqzy AC1 and AC12: 'RFC 0038 D14 gains a Hold paragraph'; description: 'the owner can override any of them'; no owner-approval AC. By contrast bu-6qaju2.1 AC7: 'owner's approval is recorded verbatim ... before merge'. bu-idcqzy AC1 and bu-6qaju2.4 Governing still cite REQ-capability-authorization-017; only notes on .1 and idcqzy carry the renumber rule. idcqzy and n92tmr have no parent epic and no reconciliation bead.

findings.title: svqpzo.3 reverses its own dependency's acceptance criterion, and the epic's reconciliation bead misses a child
findings.evidence: bu-30sah4 AC4: 'The spawn gate's fail-open behavior is unchanged (existing test kept)'. svqpzo.3 (depends on bu-30sah4): '[decision] chose one fail-closed semantics for every caller over keeping the spawn gate fail-open as bu-30sah4's acceptance item 4 does'. bu-30sah4 is parent-child of bu-svqpzo, but bu-svqpzo.6's deps omit it and its text calls it 'tracked elsewhere'.

moves.title: Carry the owner's monthly spend ceiling across the RFC 0038 switch
moves.why: The owner-set monthly ceiling and its fleet-halt banner (openspec/specs/dashboard-spend-dashboard 'Fleet-Halt Visibility'; model_routing.py check_monthly_ceiling ~3080) are enforced only in the old spawner, which the switch deletes. svqpzo.3 reported 'no RFC 0038 bead names a global monthly ceiling successor'. D10 requires every budget check to fail closed, and bu-n92tmr already carries the concurrency cap across the switch the same way.
moves.payoff: After the switch, the owner's ceiling (for example USD 150 per month) still refuses every new invocation (lead, child, monitor, research) once month-to-date spend reaches it, and the Spend page banner still appears. Without this, spend is bounded only by per-goal budgets and the research-only daily cap from 6qaju2.4.
moves.integration_points: Runner-to-session-host launch seam from bu-u5s4w8 (the same seam as bu-n92tmr). It reuses check_monthly_ceiling in src/butlers/core/model_routing.py after svqpzo.3 makes it fail closed. It is an owner-only control-plane check: not LLM-presentable, in no catalog entry or grant, applied to every origin. Research usage settles into the same ledger. bu-enbrs2 gains an edge on it. No doctrine amendment is needed, because D10 already requires fail-closed budgets.
moves.novelty: bd search 'spend ceiling' returns only closed bu-qu8ma.2. bd search 'monthly ceiling' returns nothing. rg 'ceiling|monthly|spend cap|fleet.?halt' over open-beads.tsv finds nothing relevant. rg 'monthly|fleet' over the RFC 0038 text finds no fleet spend bound. Text scans of bu-u5s4w8, bu-fkoexp, bu-0rbswe and bu-enbrs2 find no monthly or fleet-halt mention. svqpzo.3 lists the gap but no bead was filed.

grades.reason: Strong evidence and real seams. But .1 and .2 duplicate and contradict each other, the top-severity fix is stuck with no containment, and the no-enqueuer fail-open gates are left unowned.
Coherent lane, sound lineage and egress design, owner gate framed correctly. The only defects are the over-broad .4 -> .2 edge and the literal REQ number.
Detailed, substrate-correct beads. But kqme7f.6 contradicts owner choice A, kqme7f.5 over-grants third-party goals, and the Gmail track hides an owner-HOLD dependency.
Audit-driven, deduplicated against existing beads, with callback serialization (ifb1 then ctl1) and chunk and markup handling covered. The main risk is the transitive wait on bu-fg499t.
They fill real switch gaps, but n92tmr can deadlock, idcqzy amends the RFC with no owner gate, and neither has a parent epic.

lens-research-on-web.summary: Once web_research (bu-6qaju2) exists, its own rules make three of the brief's example uses hard to deliver. (1) After any web_research call the goal is exposed, and an exposed goal must render URLs inert in owner notify and in Drive Docs. So every cited answer reaches the owner with links that cannot be tapped. (2) An obligation created under exposure runs every occurrence exposed, and exposed callers only get cached mode. So a watch the lead sets up after doing research can never see a live page. (3) Third-party goals never hold web_research, so nothing triggered by an invite or an email can…

findings.title: Every research answer reaches the owner with inert citation links
findings.evidence: bu-6qaju2.4 Lineage: the broker marks the caller and goal exposed before returning. openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/capability-authorization/spec.md:153-156 (REQ-006): while exposed, notify to the owner is allowed only 'with link previews disabled and URLs rendered inert'. bu-kqme7f.1 rule 3: under exposure every URL in Doc content is written inert.
findings.detail: Research briefs on Telegram and as Google Docs, the use case Dots testers praised most, lose clickable sources. No bead covers this: bd search 'citation' and 'inert' return nothing open on the topic.

findings.title: Watches created after research are stuck in cached mode
findings.evidence: openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/core-scheduler/spec.md:33 ('an obligation created under exposure SHALL start every occurrence exposed'). RFC 0038:400 and :443. D20(d) in bu-6qaju2.1 runs exposed callers in cached mode (provider index only, no live fetch).
findings.detail: The natural flow ('find X, then watch its price') runs research first, so the schedule_create comes from an exposed lead. Every occurrence then reads the provider index only and never sees a live change.

findings.title: Web research can never be triggered by inbound third-party content
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:384 (D5: the third-party ceiling is read, non-steering record, owner notify and park-only communicate). bu-6qaju2.4 Ceilings: 'third-party goals never' hold web_research.
findings.detail: Correct for security. It means an invite cannot trigger meeting research and an email cannot trigger a scam check. Proactive features that join web data must run as a git-declared obligation, as a deterministic probe, or as an owner goal (a forwarded message starts it exposed, so research runs cached).

findings.title: Answer text is not kept, so research cannot be reused
findings.evidence: bu-6qaju2.4 Audit and its decision: the ledger records 'answer digest; not the answer text'. Study row J23 ('Reuse background research ... Lisbon trip') is Partial because 'the web research does not' carry over.

findings.title: Running research from deterministic code needs a D18 amendment
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:799-827: model functions are 'Tool-less, single-turn, structured-output calls made by deterministic code', and 'Adding a kind to this list requires an RFC amendment'. bu-6qaju2.4 lists 'web research outside goals' as a non-goal.

findings.title: Typed research-probe output is feasible with the installed Codex
findings.evidence: `codex exec --help` line 93: '--output-schema <FILE> Path to a JSON Schema file describing the model's final response shape'. bu-6qaju2.1 shows web_search='live'|'cached' as config, with every other tool disabled.
findings.detail: So a probe can return {price, currency, in_stock, ...}, and code can compare successive results without any model involved. Not verified: whether the provider accepts strict schema output together with the hosted web_search tool in one run.

findings.title: The meeting prep rail must stay a zero-LLM precompute
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py:1-15 (RFC-0020: the prep rail reads a precomputed contribution, 'NOT a per-open LLM session'; envelope at calendar/prep/<event_id>, merged through calendar.v_prep_contributions).
findings.detail: Any web context for a meeting has to be written as its own contribution ahead of time, not fetched when the owner opens the event.

findings.title: No data to drive device recall or advisory sweeps
findings.evidence: `rg -l -i manufacturer src roster --glob '*.py'` returned no files. health.medications exists (roster/health/migrations/001_health_tables.py:32), but a recall search would send medication names to the provider and to sites.
findings.detail: Candidate dropped.

moves.title: Verified citation handles: research sources render as live links even when the goal is exposed
moves.why: Without this, every research deliverable (Telegram reply, Drive Doc) has dead links, because REQ-006 and bu-kqme7f.1 rule 3 make URLs inert once a goal is exposed, and web_research always exposes it. Doctrine amendment to D20 and REQ-006: 'A URL the broker holds as a citation of a research call, taken from the research host's event stream, may be rendered live in owner notify and owner-private Drive writes; URLs written by the model stay inert and link previews stay disabled.'
moves.payoff: The owner asks on Telegram 'compare 3 standing desks under $600' and gets a reply whose [1] [2] [3] sources open with one tap, each showing its hostname. The same Doc in Drive keeps clickable sources.
moves.integration_points: bu-6qaju2.4 broker web_research: returns citation handles (research_call_id plus index) next to the citations. Switchboard research-call ledger table (citations, urls_opened). notify.v1 envelope render_links_inert (openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/butler-messenger/spec.md:52): add citation_refs that Messenger resolves server-side. Drive drive_create_doc/drive_update_doc (bu-kqme7f.1) gain citation_refs. Capability web_research, effect class read; notify is communicate to the owner; Drive is record. All origins that hold web_research.
moves.novelty: `bd search citation` and `bd search inert`: no open bead. bu-6qaju2.1/.4 do not cover rendering. bu-kqme7f.1 rule 3 makes links inert with no exception. The pursuit ledger has no research or citation moves (rg 'web|research|citation': no hits).

moves.title: Pinned research probes with standing web watches (price, availability, page or policy change)
moves.why: vision.md:5-8 says Butlers 'notices useful work before the owner asks'. Study rows F12 and J21 (price and listing watch, following a developing story) are gaps. A watch built as an obligation that runs a goal fails on the exposure rule (finding 2). A probe whose question the owner fixed, run by code, puts no goal data in front of the research model, so it can safely run live. Doctrine amendment, RFC 0038 D18: add the kind 'Pinned research probes: deterministic code sends an owner-approved fixed question and output schema to the research host; the typed output is third-party content.'
moves.payoff: Owner: 'watch the Sony WH-1000XM7 at these two shops, tell me under S$400', or 'tell me if my airline's baggage policy page changes'. A daily probe runs. When the typed price crosses the threshold, one Telegram insight arrives with live source links (move 1). No goal runs unless the owner taps 'look into it'.
moves.integration_points: New control-plane capabilities: web_watch_create and web_watch_delete (administer; per-event approval pins question, schema kind price|availability|page_digest, cadence and expiry as safety_args), web_watch_list (read). Switchboard tables web_watches and web_watch_snapshots (tainted). A job-mode schedule calls the research host client from bu-6qaju2.3 with --output-schema in live mode. On change it calls propose_insight_candidate with third-party lineage, through the insight broker's dedup, quiet hours and caps. The optional 'wake the lead' admission goes through the bu-o9qax4 obligation subm…
moves.novelty: rg 'price watch|web watch|page watch|watchlist|restock' over openspec/about/docs/roster/src: only ActivityWatch hits. `bd search watch` (open): Sheets watch bu-kqme7f.2, threshold watchers bu-60pwv6.24 (ingestion data), nothing for the web. `bd search probe`: no research probes. Study F12 is marked GAP with no bead.

moves.title: Public context for external organisations in meeting prep
moves.why: The prep rail already joins attendees, last met and open commitments (src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py:20-48). It has no outside context, which Dots offers for meeting prep (study J42). Butlers can add context about the organisation while disclosing only a company domain, never a person, title or agenda. Needs move 2's probe kind (D18 amendment).
moves.payoff: Before a 10:00 call with two people from acme-robotics.com, the prep rail and the morning brief show 'Acme Robotics: warehouse AMRs; raised Series C on 2026-10-02; CEO change in Sept', with source links, beside the existing 'last met' and 'you owe them the deck'.
moves.integration_points: A deterministic job (daily 06:30) picks the next 48h of events whose attendees resolve to non-owner entities with a company email domain. The question comes from a code template ('What does <domain> do; notable news in the last 30 days'). Probe through move 2's runner in live mode. Results are written as a contribution key calendar/prep-public/<event_id> merged by calendar.v_prep_contributions (core_142), plus an organisation-entity public_context record (tainted), with a 14-day per-domain cache. The research call itself sits outside any goal, so no goal origin or grant is involved; the owner…
moves.novelty: rg 'meeting prep|pre-meeting|meeting brief': only calendar_workspace and calendar_prep (internal data, zero-LLM). Open beads: bu-2jtfw.14 (attendee links), bu-8cdl1.8 (entity dossier, internal); none with web context. Ledger run 15 #12 is the post-meeting debrief, not prep.

moves.title: Trip destination brief from booked trips
moves.why: The Travel MANIFESTO is about making time-sensitive actions visible. travel.documents only tracks visa, insurance, boarding pass and receipt expiry (roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py:138-147); nothing checks entry rules, local holidays or advisories for the trip's dates. Butlers holds the structured trip; Dots must infer it from mail. Needs move 2's probe kind.
moves.payoff: 21 days before the Lisbon trip (Nov 12-18), one insight: 'Entry: no visa for your passport, EES biometric registration on arrival; Nov 15 local holiday, museums closed; plugs type F; no advisory change.' A refresh at 3 days out flags only differences.
moves.integration_points: A job in the travel region reads travel.trips (destination, dates) and legs (arrival airport). Owner nationality comes from the owner entity's nationality fact (functional predicate, roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:2486), opt-in only. Three code-templated probes run in live mode. Output is a tainted trip_brief record linked to trip_id and proposed through propose_insight_candidate; the pre-trip-checklist skill can read it. The research runs outside any goal; reading the brief exposes the reader.
moves.novelty: rg 'visa|entry requirement|advisory|public holiday' in roster/travel: only document expiry and pg advisory locks. Skills trip-planner and pre-trip-checklist have no web step. Open beads: none (rg 'travel' with web/brief: none). Study J23 covers memory reuse only.

moves.title: Owner-approved live research when a goal is exposed
moves.why: D20(d) silently downgrades an exposed goal to cached mode. Once a goal has read one email, live prices, availability and news are out of reach, and the owner is never told. Asking the owner keeps the exfiltration guard and restores freshness. Doctrine amendment, D20(d): 'An exposed caller may request live mode; the broker parks the call for per-event owner approval showing the exact question; on approval it runs live with the question pinned.'
moves.payoff: In a goal that summarised a vendor email, the lead needs today's price. The owner gets a Telegram card 'Live web search will send: "current price Herman Miller Aeron size B Singapore" [Approve] [Use cached]'. One tap gets a fresh answer.
moves.integration_points: web_research gains an optional request_live boolean (honoured only when exposed). The broker parks through the RFC 0021 approval path (pending_actions) with the question as a safety_arg. Telegram signed callback approve/reject (bu-z0b0ah.5 surface). The research-call ledger records mode=live_approved. Effect class read, approval-gated only on this path. Owner and obligation goals that hold web_research; never third-party.
moves.novelty: bu-6qaju2.1 D20(d) and bu-6qaju2.4 set the mode from exposure with 'no argument selects it'. No bead offers an approval path. `bd search` for live/approval combinations finds nothing open on research.

moves.title: Research library: cited answers kept as dated, tainted records the lead can reuse
moves.why: Study J23 (reuse earlier destination research) is a gap, and repeated questions spend again. bu-6qaju2.4 deliberately keeps only a digest. Keeping the answer as a tainted record follows the existing D6 taint model and needs no doctrine change.
moves.payoff: In March the owner asks for Lisbon neighbourhood research. In October, 'plan Lisbon' recalls it ('from 2026-03-04, 4 sources; refresh?') at zero spend, and the owner can browse or delete past research on the goal page.
moves.integration_points: Add answer_text, with a retention setting, to the bu-6qaju2.4 Switchboard research-call table. New research_recall capability (read, output_trust stamped, each item tainted) searchable by context.search. A D19 goal-page list with delete. runtime_config research.library_retention_days (default 180). Owner and obligation grants.
moves.novelty: bu-6qaju2.4 decision 'answer digest instead of the answer text'. `bd search` 'research library' and 'reuse': none. Memory docs have no research note type (rg 'research' in docs/modules/memory.md: none checked beyond the ledger). Also filed as ledger_feedback on bu-6qaju2.4.

measurements.metric: Open beads that cover web watches, citation rendering or research reuse
measurements.evidence: rg -i 'watch|price|news|brief|research|web' open-beads.tsv; bd search citation / inert / watch / probe
WebSearch on codex exec --output-schema; local `codex exec --help` line 93 confirms the flag

lens-comms-delegate.summary:
The filed beads cover the Gmail reach: read and modify (bu-kqme7f.5), and draft or reply in-thread (bu-kqme7f.6). They do not cover the four things that turn that reach into a working chief of staff.

1. **A safe way to approve repeated low-risk replies.** RFC 0038 D13 allows only template-pinned standing rules for exposed invocations, and every reply drafted after reading a thread is exposed (D6). The rules engine supports only exact, pattern and any constraints (rules.py:7-9), and no bead builds template pinning. Without it, every reply parks forever.
2. **A two-way promise ledger.** The co…

findings.title: Template-pinned standing rules are specified but have no constraint type and no builder
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/rules.py:7-9,55-73 (exact|pattern|any only); RFC 0038 D13 lines 716-723; openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/capability-authorization/spec.md:162-168; `bd search template-pinned` -> []; bu-cadcr1 only matches rules (lines 27-28,145)
findings.detail: Under exposure only owner-recipient or template-pinned rules exempt a send. Every Gmail reply is exposed because it follows a thread read, so bu-kqme7f.6's 'or an owner-created standing rule' path cannot be reached for non-owner replies.

findings.title: Approval fatigue for replies is structural: promotion fingerprints exact arguments, and exposed approvals never count
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/autonomy_suggestions.py:27-40 (scope comes from exact v2 fingerprint arguments); RFC 0038 D6 lines 465-466 (exposed approvals do not count toward promotion)
findings.detail: Free-text bodies never repeat exactly, so the RFC 0021 ladder can never offer a rule for replies. Each confirmation or acknowledgement needs its own tap.

findings.title: The commitments ledger supports other_to_owner, but nothing writes it from messages
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/commitments.py:129; `rg -l other_to_owner src roster` (non-test) -> only api/models/calendar_workspace.py, jobs/calendar_prep.py, core/entity_graph_edges.py (readers); roster/relationship/tools/commitments.py:151,601 (owner_to_other from owner utterances only)
findings.detail: Nothing tracks what other people promised the owner, or what the owner promised them in WhatsApp, Telegram or email. The Relationship manifesto says 'The one who follows through' (MANIFESTO.md:41).

findings.title: Spec drift: the Telegram user-client spec says it captures commitments, but no commitment writer exists
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/connector-telegram-user-client/spec.md:4 ('butlers gain awareness of life events, commitments, ...'); the commitment-capture skill covers only owner utterances (roster/relationship/.claude/skills/commitment-capture/SKILL.md:21-22)

findings.title: The Gmail connector fetches the owner's archive and label actions, then discards them
findings.evidence: src/butlers/connectors/gmail.py:2093-2094 ('History records contain messagesAdded, messagesDeleted, labelsAdded, labelsRemoved / We only care about messagesAdded')
findings.detail: These records show the owner's real triage behaviour at zero extra API cost, and they could drive learned, inspectable triage rules.

findings.title: Owner-authorship signals already exist on every outbound channel
findings.evidence: gmail.py:803-844 (lists in:sent newer_than:7d, metadata Message-ID); whatsapp_user_client.py:1808-1823 (raw.is_from_me per message); telegram_user_client.py:1156-1157 (owner tag per message); connectors/owner_outbound_events.py:1-30
findings.detail: Owner-written spans can be told apart from third-party text without a model. This supports promise extraction and voice learning without trusting third-party content.

findings.title: Bulk-mail signals are parsed for tiering and then dropped
findings.evidence: src/butlers/connectors/gmail_policy.py:242-258 (List-Unsubscribe, Precedence bulk); `bd search newsletter|unsubscribe --status all` -> []

findings.title: Approving an edited draft overwrites the original arguments; the change survives only as an audit note
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:3127-3150 (tool_args.update(edits); edits_note=json.dumps(edits))
findings.detail: The owner's corrections to drafts are the strongest style signal available. Today they are kept only as unstructured audit JSON.

findings.title: Telegram already has HMAC-verified owner decision callbacks that a one-tap confirm can reuse
findings.evidence: src/butlers/connectors/telegram_bot.py:1033-1107 (approval HMAC), 1155-1208 (decision HMAC)
findings.detail: Moves 2-4 can turn tainted candidates into owner-authority records through an existing non-grantable owner-decision path, with no new trust root.

moves.title: Standing replies: owner-authored, template-pinned reply rules with typed slots
moves.why: RFC 0038 D13 and REQ-capability-authorization-006 make template-pinned rules the only standing rules an exposed invocation can use, and every in-thread reply is exposed (D6). rules.py has no template type, so bu-kqme7f.6 replies to non-owners always park: approval fatigue is built into the design. No doctrine amendment is needed; this implements D13 as written.
moves.payoff: The owner writes a template once on the dashboard: 'Confirmed, see you {date} at {time}.' to Sam, or 'Thanks, received.' to the accountant, capped at 5 sends a week for 90 days. When a later sweep or owner goal reads Sam's 'does Thu 7:30 work?', the reply goes out at once and the owner gets the receipt 'Sent standing reply to Sam: Confirmed, see you Thu 17 Oct at 19:30. [Revoke rule]'. After three approved near-identical replies, Butlers offers the template text for the owner to accept or edit.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/approvals/rules.py: a new constraint type {type:'template', text, slots:{name: date|time|datetime|amount|integer|identifier}} compiled to an anchored grammar, plus an is_template_pinned(rule) classifier. A free-text slot or any unconstrained content-bearing argument (subject, body) fails the classifier. The rule is authored only through the owner-decision path (dashboard or HMAC Telegram), never grantable (D4). The broker match in bu-cadcr1 uses the classifier. Capabilities: gmail_send_reply (bu-kqme7f.6, communicate, recipient_params to and cc), with the recipient pinned …
moves.novelty: `bd search template-pinned` -> []. `rg template rules.py` -> none. awk over open-beads.tsv for approv|template|standing|promotion|batch -> no template builder (bu-cadcr1 consumes, bu-h40h2b.11 Standing Orders page, bu-27dxl.4.6 rule loop). The pursuit ledger has no 'standing repl' or 'template' move.

moves.title: Promise radar: two-way commitments from the owner's own messages and from counterparties' promises, confirmed with one tap
moves.why: The chief-of-staff 'waiting on' and 'you promised' lists. The ledger already has other_to_owner (core/commitments.py:129) but no message-derived writer, and commitment-capture covers only owner-to-butler utterances. Relationship MANIFESTO:41 promises 'the one who follows through'. Dots cannot see WhatsApp or Telegram. No doctrine amendment: REQ-commitment-lifecycle-007 forbids owner-authority commitments from exposed invocations, so candidates stay tainted until the owner taps.
moves.payoff: Thursday evening on Telegram: 'You told Sam on WhatsApp (Tue) you would send the deck Fri. Track it? [Track] [Done] [Ignore]'. On Tuesday: 'Still waiting on Ali's quote (promised by email for Mon). [Draft a nudge] [+3 days] [Drop]'. Draft a nudge produces a parked reply through bu-kqme7f.6, or a standing reply from move 1.
moves.integration_points: Relationship region. New table relationship.commitment_candidates: direction, counterparty entity resolved from the connector sender identity rather than a capitalised name, action text of at most 120 characters, due date, evidence ref to the ingestion event id, taint stamp, and no raw body. Capability commitment_candidate_propose (record, non-steering, allowed under the third_party ceiling, D5). Owner-authored spans are detected deterministically from is_from_me and the owner tag (whatsapp_user_client.py:1819, telegram_user_client.py:1156) and run through the existing marker gate in roster/r…

lens-errand-prep.summary: The best handoff design is a deterministic "door": a vendor link Butlers creates from an owner-confirmed registry, never from model text. Under RFC 0038, every errand prep that read a receipt email or web research is exposed, and owner notify must render all its URLs inert (core-notify spec:196-209). Without doors, "owner taps once" cannot work for exactly the errands that need it. Telegram URL buttons accept only HTTP(S) or tg://, so "open in the vendor's own app" means vendor https universal links that come from the registry. Today the subscription cancellation door (bu-8cdl1.10, closed) is…

findings.title: Any session, including one handling third-party email, can overwrite the owner's subscription cancellation door
findings.evidence: roster/finance/tools/subscriptions.py:52,89-91 (cancellation_url free TEXT, 'may be populated later by owner enrichment'); :137 `cancellation_url = COALESCE($9, cancellation_url)` on an upsert keyed only by (service, frequency) at :119-123; finance_jobs.py:1357-1361 puts it in the owner insight as 'Cancel by ... at {cancellation_url}'; grep finds no URL/domain validation helper in src/ or roster/
findings.detail: A phishing 'manage your Netflix plan' email routed to Finance can set or replace the door. The next renewal warning then sends the owner to the attacker's page.

findings.title: An email can set subscription status to cancelled and silence the 'never an un-warned renewal' promise
findings.evidence: subscriptions.py:132 `status = $4` is unconditional on update; Finance MANIFESTO.md:20 'We will never let a subscription renew without warning you first'
findings.detail: Status is not checked against provenance. A spoofed 'your subscription was cancelled' email stops the warnings even though the bank keeps being charged.

findings.title: RFC 0038 makes one-tap handoff impossible for exposed errand prep unless the link comes from somewhere other than the model
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:308 (exposed owner notify only with 'URLs rendered inert'); openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/core-notify/spec.md:196-209; bu-6qaju2.4 design: web_research marks the caller exposed
findings.detail: Receipts, order emails and web research are third-party content. A shortlist or return pack built from them can reach the owner only with inert links.

findings.title: The inert-link rule covers message text but not Telegram URL buttons
findings.evidence: core-notify spec.md:197 ('every URL in the message'); src/butlers/telegram_api.py:57-86 (the validator checks only callback_data, so url buttons pass unchecked); src/butlers/modules/telegram.py:258-265 (telegram_send_message takes model-supplied reply_markup; approval-gated on Messenger, roster/messenger/butler.toml:78)
findings.detail: Messenger's render_links_inert handling (tasks.md 2.13) must also strip or refuse url, login_url and web_app buttons. Otherwise a gated or future path can carry a live link outside the text.

findings.title: Before cutover, URLs in owner Telegram messages are live and previewed
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/telegram.py:442-446 (sendMessage payload has no link_preview_options); Telegram Bot API LinkPreviewOptions.is_disabled ('True, if the link preview is disabled', core.telegram.org/bots/api)
findings.detail: Combined with finding 1, an email-sourced URL is clickable and fetched for a preview today. Fixing this is allowed on the frozen path.

findings.title: Telegram URL buttons accept only HTTP or tg:// URLs
findings.evidence: core.telegram.org/bots/api InlineKeyboardButton.url: 'HTTP or tg:// URL to be opened when the button is pressed.'
findings.detail: To open the vendor's own app, a door must be the vendor's https universal or app link. Custom schemes like grab:// cannot be buttons, which makes the registry's https host the anti-phishing anchor.

findings.title: The expected_refund cost-claim kind exists but has no producer and no owner surface
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_239_cost_claims.py:62-64 (kind includes 'expected_refund'); src/butlers/core_tools/_cost_claims.py:17-25 (assertable); rg 'expected_refund' finds no producer; roster/finance/jobs/finance_jobs.py:49-52 (the sweep proposes no insight); RFC 0033 non-goals: 'No owner UI, approval verbs, insight/condition wiring'

findings.title: No guard for charges after a subscription is cancelled

findings.detail: A merchant that keeps billing after cancellation is caught only by generic anomaly detection, if at all, and with no dispute evidence attached.

findings.title: Purchases have no return or warranty windows; the idea was deferred twice and never filed

findings.title: The doctrine's 'prepared actions' clause is ambiguous for handoff links
findings.evidence: about/heart-and-soul/security.md:78-80 ('transact ... disabled for every goal, including as prepared actions')

lens-documents.summary: Butlers takes in documents but cannot read most of them. Telegram photos and documents become blobs, and Gmail records PDF, sheet and docx attachment metadata. But a PDF over about 48 KB cannot be read: get_attachment refuses anything over 64 KB of base64 and attachment_view accepts only image/* files. Gmail attachments are never fetched, because attachment_materialize was never built and GmailConnector.fetch_attachment has no callers. So the Finance promise to read "every invoice" fails for every real PDF bill. The study's claim that "reading works" is wrong. Six moves follow, all built on R…

findings.title: Every deadline taken from a document would need a per-event approval after the switch
findings.evidence: openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/deadline-tracking/spec.md:4 catalogs deadline_create, deadline_update and deadline_delete as administer outright; RFC 0038 D5 table line 384: a third_party origin never gets administer

moves.why: Travel MANIFESTO.md:13,24 promise everything in one place by the airport. travel.documents.blob_ref (001_travel_tables.py:143) holds originals that are never handed back. Owner value M.

All of it is in Telegram's offline cache at the gate.

Capability effect class record, owner-private.

lens-long-goals.summary: Nothing in RFC 0038 or the filed beads covers work that lasts weeks. A goal is bounded by its budget and deadline (D10) and cannot be resumed (D9). Continuity is one carry-forward text blob per scheduled task (core-scheduler delta, lines 144-191). Fleet cases are situations the system notices, and no model or dashboard action may open a free-form one (bu-h40h2b.8, Slice C). After cutover, every self-scheduled follow-up is an `administer` effect that needs the owner's approval (RFC 0038:311, 545-546; settled in bu-4m4e42). So a multi-week project today would mean a tap for every check-in, a wo…

findings.title: No unit of work outlives one goal
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:627-640 (D10: a budget per goal with a deadline; exhaustion ends the goal); :622-624 (D9: 'There is no resume'); openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/core-scheduler/spec.md:144-191 (continuity is one live carry_forward row per butler and task); rg 'project|initiative|multi-week' in goal-orchestration spec, design.md and open-beads.tsv: no matches
findings.detail: A multi-week project (moving house, a job search) has no object that holds its plan, groups its goals, caps total spend, or can be stopped as a whole. Dots sells exactly this: 'take a project from an idea to work you can use' (dots_core_product.md:31).

findings.title: Fleet cases cannot be the project container
findings.evidence: bu-h40h2b.8 design, Slice C: 'no LLM/dash action may open a free-form case'; openspec/specs/fleet-case-file/spec.md:13,56 (one non-closed case per correlation_key; Switchboard is the only writer)
findings.detail: Situations are noticed by the system. Projects are authored by the owner. They should link to each other (one project, many cases), not merge.

findings.title: Every project follow-up costs an approval tap after cutover
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:545-546 (prompt-mode schedule_create becomes obligation creation, an administer capability); :383 (the obligation default grant has no administer); :311 (administer needs per-event approval and is never delegable); owner settlement recorded in bu-4m4e42 and the dots study memory
findings.detail: If nothing bundles the approvals, a six-week project with twice-weekly check-ins plus ad hoc follow-ups means a dozen or more administer taps. Bundling must happen when the project's charter is approved, without weakening the settled rule.

findings.title: A shared project log exposes every later check-in
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:445-452 (D6: 'text that an exposed goal stored from an email exposes whichever later goal reads it back'); :296 (an owner_authority record is refused under exposure)
findings.detail: One check-in that stores a landlord's email or a web result in the project state makes every later check-in exposed. Exposed check-ins cannot then edit owner-authority plan fields. That is the right block against prompt injection, but only if the plan (the charter) and the evidence log are stored separately.

findings.title: Exposed check-ins get only cached web research
findings.evidence: bu-6qaju2.4 (research mode 'is cached when the calling invocation is exposed at call time, live otherwise'; the broker 'marks the calling invocation and its goal exposed' after each call)
findings.detail: A project price watch or listing watch that reads its tainted log first can never do live research. One that researches first gets one live call per invocation. The workaround is to delegate charter-only children before reading anything tainted. No bead or lead policy documents this ordering.

findings.title: An owner's reply to a check-in may arrive after the goal has ended
findings.evidence: bu-fkoexp settles 'how an owner's reply to an outbound prompt joins the goal that sent it'; D11 (RFC 0038:642-660) lets an obligation goal complete after its notify
findings.detail: Project check-in goals finish within minutes. The owner answers on Telegram days later, so the reply has to bind to the project (server-held) rather than to the finished goal.

findings.title: 'Handing a project between regions' does not apply under D19
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:829-850 (one mind, regions are not agents); :601-620 (the lead calls capabilities directly; the cross-butler delegation ledger is removed, :932-933)
findings.detail: A project spans regions through a declared capability set. It needs one owning region for its own records and obligations (REQ-goal-orchestration-007 says domains own obligations). General is the fit: its MANIFESTO.md:41 says 'Organize by project'.

findings.title: Most project building blocks already exist
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/temporal/deadlines_db.py:71-80 (deadlines with depends_on and alert thresholds); src/butlers/core/commitments.py:424-440 (owner condition ledger with counterparty and deadline); roster/travel/AGENTS.md:12,23 (trip containers planned→active→completed); src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1485-1489 (candidate rule endorse); src/butlers/core_tools/_scheduling.py:78-79 (end_at/until_at)
findings.detail: A project can be mostly links plus a charter. Milestones can be deadlines and commitments, and expiry can use until_at. No new task engine is needed.

findings.title: Projects are outside the v1 scope list
findings.evidence: about/heart-and-soul/v1.md:3-4 ('If a capability is not named here, it waits'); v1.md:33-36 (module list)
findings.detail: Adding owner projects needs a one-line v1 scope amendment naming the capability.

findings.title: Dots' known weakness on long work is opaque progress
findings.evidence: .tmp/dots-case-study/research_notes/ChatGPT Dots capability gap study/dots_control_safety_limits.md:269 ('repeatedly reports progress but fails to complete tasks or clearly disclose that work has stopped'); dots_hands_on_reviews.md:98 (no reviewer saw a dot work for hours on one task with visible progress)
findings.detail: An honest project ledger (what ran, what each run spent, what is waiting on the owner, an armed or disarmed state) is a structural lead Butlers can claim over Dots.

moves.title: Owner Projects: a durable charter that groups goals, obligations and links
moves.why: vision.md:10 promises 'a whole goal across life domains', but D9 and D10 bound every goal to minutes. A charter only the owner can change gives the owner what Dots sells as a 'project' (dots_core_product.md:31), with memory the owner can inspect.
moves.payoff: The owner says on Telegram 'start a project: move to Tiong Bahru by Dec 15, budget S$4k, must keep the Mon/Wed gym'. From then on every related goal, trip, commitment, deadline and situation shows on one /projects/:id page, and Stop pauses all of it.
moves.integration_points: General region, roster/general/migrations: general.projects (id, kind, title, state draft|armed|paused|closed, charter jsonb with an owner_authority stamp, horizon_end, budget_envelope) and general.project_links (typed refs to goal, travel.trip, commitment, deadline task, fleet_case, drive file). The goal ledger (bu-fkoexp) gains a nullable project_ref set only from server-held context. Capabilities: project.read (read, stamped); project.create and project.charter_set (record, owner_authority=true, so refused under exposure); project.link (record). Owner goals hold all of these; obligation go…
moves.novelty: rg 'project|workspace|initiative|multi-week' in open-beads.tsv: only unrelated hits ('projection', 'project-shape'). Same search in pursuit-ledger.md: none. Goal-orchestration spec and design.md: none. bu-h40h2b.8 Situations covers system-noticed cases and forbids free-form opens, so it is a neighbour, not a duplicate. General collections (roster/general/AGENTS.md) have no lifecycle, grants or goal linkage.

moves.title: One approval arms a project's whole check-in plan
moves.why: The owner settled that follow-ups a schedule-origin goal creates need approval (bu-4m4e42; RFC 0038:311,383,545). This move keeps that rule exactly while cutting the tap count to one per project plus explicit extras, versus Dots' self-chosen wake-ups (study R5).
moves.payoff: Creating the moving project produces one Telegram approval card: 'Check in Mon and Thu 08:00 until Dec 15. Wake 3 days before each milestone you set. Read calendar, finance, travel and email. Up to 4 live web searches a week. Envelope S$6 of model spend. Approve?' One tap arms everything, and it all disarms on its own after Dec 15.
moves.integration_points: An administer capability project.arm (per-event approval, never delegable) whose parked call shows the full obligation bundle in the D13 approval: scheduled_tasks rows tagged project_ref with until_at=horizon_end; a declared capability set (region reads, project.read/link/log_append, owner notify, optional web_research per bu-6qaju2.4, which obligation goals hold only when declared); a budget envelope. Check-in obligation goals hold no administer. An extra wake goes through project.request_wake, which parks an administer effect for one tap. Milestone-anchored wakes fire from deadlines only wh…
moves.novelty: Study row 3c (report:331) proposed letting goals self-schedule one follow-up without approval, and the owner rejected that. This move is the approved-once alternative and is not filed. rg 'pre-author|check-in|cadence|envelope' in open-beads.tsv and pursuit-ledger.md: no project-scoped hit. bu-kqme7f.3 is one fixed git-declared monitor, not an obligation bundle the owner arms per project. bu-idcqzy is a fleet-wide hold, not a per-project one.

moves.title: Living brief and decision log, with the charter stored apart from tainted evidence
moves.why: D6 taint survives storage (RFC 0038:445-452). A single shared brief would expose every later check-in, which blocks plan edits and forces cached-only research (bu-6qaju2.4). Separating them keeps the plan trusted and the evidence auditable.
moves.payoff: Every check-in starts from the owner's own charter. The brief shows 'state as of Thu', open questions, and a decision log such as 'Movers: A S$1.2k vs B S$950 (B has no insurance, cited); recommendation A; your verdict: pending'. The owner taps a verdict, and the decision becomes durable, cited project history.
moves.integration_points: general.project_log (append-only entries: kind state|note|question|decision_option; stamps; source refs; written by project.log_append, record, tainted under exposure) and general.project_decisions (question, options with evidence refs, recommendation, owner_verdict). project.decision_propose is a record. The verdict is recorded only through a signed Telegram callback or the dashboard (an owner-decision path, never LLM-presentable, D4). The check-in lead policy, delivered as General region guidance via guidance.load, reads the charter first, then delegates live-research children from charter-…
moves.novelty: rg 'living brief|decision log|decision_log' in open-beads.tsv and the ledger: only bu-lsxqb0.21 (RFC decision records, unrelated). task_continuity (core-scheduler spec:144-191) is one untyped blob per task with no charter or evidence split and no decisions. Ledger run 11 #7 'Fleet Case File' holds evidence but has no owner charter or verdicts.

moves.title: Telegram project card with reply-binding and per-project controls
moves.why: Telegram is the phone surface to optimize (epic bu-z0b0ah). Dots' weak spot is opaque progress (dots_control_safety_limits.md:269), and an honest card per project is visibly better.
moves.payoff: Each check-in sends at most one card: 'Move · at risk · next: movers booked by Nov 3 (5 days) · 2 decisions waiting', with buttons [On track] [Snooze a week] [Pause] [Close]. Replying 'go with A, book survey' binds to the project without the owner naming it. /projects lists active projects with their next wake.
moves.integration_points: Messenger notify to the owner (inert links under exposure, D4) with a project card template. Reply binding: the Telegram reply_to_message_id maps to project_ref in a server-held table that admission reads (extends bu-fkoexp's outbound-prompt join). The /projects command is handled deterministically by the control plane, like bu-z0b0ah.5. Pause, Snooze and Close are owner-decision callbacks (signed, never LLM-presentable). Snooze shifts occurrences inside the approved bundle and never extends until_at. The D19 overview (bu-k2z6iw) gets a projects strip.
moves.novelty: bu-z0b0ah.1-.5 cover long replies, files, links, progress and /status /stop /hold /resume, all fleet-wide or per goal. None is per project. bu-kqme7f.4 adds insight feedback buttons, not project controls. rg 'project card|/projects' in open-beads.tsv: none.

moves.title: Project close-out: a retrospective that becomes owner-endorsable memory
moves.why: The health manifesto says life is 'a story told over weeks' (roster/health/MANIFESTO.md:7), and memory the owner can inspect is where Butlers is ahead of Dots (study R18). A close-out turns the lessons of one project into rules the owner can endorse for the next one.
moves.payoff: On close, the owner gets: 'Moved Dec 14 (1 day early); spent S$3.6k of S$4k; 3 decisions; the movers survey took 9 days.' Two proposed lessons follow, such as 'next move: book a survey 6 weeks out'. The owner taps Endorse on one, and the next moving project loads it automatically.
moves.integration_points: A project.close owner decision triggers one close-out obligation goal (origin obligation, declared set: project.read, region reads such as finance spend over the horizon, memory store_episode and propose_rule as record, owner notify). Rules are written at maturity 'candidate' with non-owner authority. The owner endorses them through the existing POST /api/memory/rules/{id}/endorse (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1485-1489). The project row stores the outcome, and the obligation bundle is disarmed in the same transaction.
moves.novelty: rg 'retrospect|close-out|lessons' in open-beads.tsv and the ledger: none. Chronicler (RFC 0014) narrates days, not projects. Candidate rules and endorse exist (memory.py:1485-1489), so the new part is only the project trigger and its scope.

moves.title: Decision projects: compare options and hand off a buy-ready packet without buying
moves.why: No purchases ever (owner decision 8, RFC 0038:1036), but prep-and-handoff is allowed. This covers J16, J29 and J45, which the study scored Partial (gap_matrix_reach_actions.md:257,270,286), with data Dots lacks: real budget headroom, the calendar for delivery, and home specs.
moves.payoff: 'Help me choose a robot vacuum under S$900; the flat has 2 rugs.' Over two weeks the project builds an options matrix against the owner's criteria. It watches prices twice a week within the envelope, checks finance headroom and the calendar for delivery, then sends 'decision-ready: X at S$849, a 12% drop'. The buy link appears on the dashboard; Butlers never pays.
moves.integration_points: Project kind 'decision': charter criteria (owner_authority), options and evidence in project_decisions (move 3). A web_research child is declared in the arm bundle (bu-6qaju2.4; obligation goals need it named). Region reads: finance budgets and balances, calendar, home. Price observations are stamped untrusted log entries. The handoff packet is a dashboard view with links live only there; Telegram links stay inert under exposure (D4).
moves.novelty: rg 'price|purchase|shortlist|wishlist' in open-beads.tsv: only unrelated hits (Gemini prices, runtime handoffs). rg -il 'wishlist|shortlist' over roster/ and src/: none. The study names J16, J29 and J45 as Partial with web research as the only gap, but none is filed as a project-shaped capability.

lens-phone-ambient.summary: Butlers ingests the owner's location (OwnTracks points, region transitions, movement episodes), home state (HA snapshots, owner presence) and calendar. It also already has the pieces of an always-at-hand phone loop: signed Telegram approval callbacks, context-bus holds, and the RFC 0028 actuation risk map. What it lacks is phone-native use of them. The bot calls 9 Bot API methods (getUpdates, setWebhook, deleteWebhook, sendMessage, editMessageText, editMessageReplyMarkup, answerCallbackQuery, setMessageReaction, getFile). It uses no web_app or Mini App, setChatMenuButton, pinChatMessage, answ…

findings.title: Telegram bot ignores every Mini App and ambient Bot API surface
findings.evidence: rg of /(editMessageText|sendChatAction|sendDocument|sendPhoto|setMyCommands|setChatMenuButton|answerInlineQuery|sendLocation|sendVenue|pinChatMessage|sendPoll|deleteMessage|answerWebAppQuery) over src/ and roster/ finds only editMessageText and editMessageReplyMarkup (src/butlers/telegram_api.py:99,120). Calls in use: getUpdates (telegram_bot.py:695), setWebhook, answerCallbackQuery (:1507), getFile (:1644), sendMessage (modules/telegram.py:441), setMessageReaction (:567). rg for 'web_app|WebApp|initData|mini app' over src/, frontend/, openspec/, about/ and docs/ finds 0 hits.
findings.detail: Bot API 6.0 menu-button launch, 7.2 BiometricManager, 8.0 LocationManager and addToHomeScreen, 9.0 SecureStorage are all available (https://core.telegram.org/bots/webapps) and none is used.

findings.title: Shared location, venue and contact lose their payload in normalized text
findings.evidence: src/butlers/connectors/telegram_bot.py:145-157 maps location to '[Location]'. :205-211 keeps only the name of a contact, dropping the phone number. Venue has no label at all. The raw update rides along at :1897-1898, but the model works from normalized_text.
findings.detail: A dropped pin ('this is the climbing gym', 'I parked here') can't become a named place or a fact.

findings.title: Owner message edits and Telegram live-location updates are silently deduped away
findings.evidence: telegram_bot.py:1835 ingests edited_message. The idempotency key at :1863-1867 is tg:<chat_id>:<message_id>, the same as the original message, and openspec/specs/connector-telegram-bot/spec.md:217-220 says duplicate accepted ingest is treated as success.
findings.detail: Edits that correct a time ('oops, 8pm not 7pm') never reach Butlers, and live-location shares can't drive an ETA.

findings.title: Forwarded third-party text arrives as owner-authored on the bot connector
findings.evidence: rg 'forward_origin|forward_from|is_forward' over src/ and roster/ *.py finds 0 connector hits. telegram_bot.py:1853-1855 sets sender to msg.from (the owner). RFC 0038:397-398 requires connector-marked forwarded spans to start the goal exposed.
findings.detail: Already filed as bu-xmueeq, but that bead's delta list omits connector-telegram-bot (see ledger_feedback).

findings.title: No owner-authored place, arrival or departure trigger exists anywhere
findings.evidence: OwnTracks transition and waypoint events are ingested (owntracks.py:116, :650-655). Context bus vocabulary is limited to at_home, commuting and similar (context_bus.py:21-35), used only for holds (attention_ledger.py:548-597). rg 'location_reminder|place_trigger|when I (arrive|get to|leave)|geofence' over src/, roster/, openspec/, about/ and docs/ finds 0. bd search for arrive, departure and location finds no such bead.
findings.detail: Run 11 #11 (bu-8cdl1.11, closed) built presence with arrival lead time, but only to gate delivery, never to fire anything.

findings.title: No departure sweep for an unsecured home
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/butler-home/spec.md:37-39 only notifies on an unexpected lock or cover state change. No job checks open covers, unlocked locks or lights left on when at_home clears (context_producers.py:420-424 just clears the signal). bd search 'away' and 'departure' find no such bead.

findings.title: Short polling at 1s instead of long polling
findings.evidence: telegram_bot.py:695 sends params {'timeout': 0}. :255 and :294 set the poll interval default to 1.0s.
findings.detail: That is up to 1s of receipt latency and about 86k getUpdates calls a day. Long polling (timeout=25-50) gives near-instant receipt at a fraction of the calls, which helps bu-2an2p and bu-z0b0ah.4.

findings.title: Place definitions are operator env config, not owner-editable
findings.evidence: context_producers.py:630-653 reads the OWNTRACKS_PLACE_REFERENCES env var. bu-x7x1r4 (owner editor for SSID places) is still blocked.
findings.detail: Every place-aware feature needs an owner-editable named-place store, and a Telegram pin is the natural way to create one.

findings.title: Approvals on the phone lack lineage; D19 requires it
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:851-853 says approvals carry lineage (goal, invocation, exposure, exact call). The Telegram approval path is a signed callback button plus a 'Review:' link to /approvals/{id}, which bu-z0b0ah.3 rates as not phone-usable (notifications.py:97-103, _routing.py:641).
findings.detail: After cutover every exposed communicate call parks per-event (RFC 0038:309), so approval volume rises, and the owner can't see on the phone what they are approving.

moves.title: Telegram Mini App as the owner's phone console: approve with lineage, Stop goals, inspect and correct memory
moves.why: D19 (RFC 0038:851-853) requires approvals to carry lineage, and cutover makes every exposed communicate park per-event (RFC 0038:309), yet the phone path is a summary button plus a dashboard link bu-z0b0ah.3 calls unusable. A Mini App launched from the chat menu button and from each approval or insight brings the D19 pages into Telegram with no separate login, which Dots cannot do over the owner's whole life.
moves.payoff: The owner taps 'Open' on 'Send reply to Sam?', sees goal, origin, exposure ('read 1 email from sam@...'), the exact call and its arguments, and approves with Face ID in the chat. The bot's menu button opens Now / Goals (with Stop) / Waiting / Memory, where 'why do you think I'm vegetarian?' shows the fact, its source and a Correct button.
moves.integration_points: New FastAPI route under src/butlers/api/owner_auth/ that validates Telegram initData (HMAC-SHA256 keyed by HMAC('WebAppData', bot token)) and resolves from.id via resolve_owner_channel_via_definer (telegram_bot.py:1063). It mints a short-lived owner session with a 'telegram_webapp' scope. The frontend is a /tg route shell reusing the bu-vvsfi8 D19 pages, loading telegram-web-app.js. The bot calls setChatMenuButton and adds web_app inline buttons in the approval and notify formatting (core_tools/_routing.py:641). No new goal capability: these are owner principal calls (RFC 0038:527, origin own…
moves.novelty: rg 'mini app|miniapp|web_app|WebApp|initData' over src/, frontend/, openspec/, about/, docs/ and the dots-case-study: 0 hits. bd search 'mini app': 0. Ledger grep 'mini app|web app|webapp|menu button': 0. Related but distinct: bu-z0b0ah.3 (phone-usable links), bu-h40h2b.10 (phone posture), bu-vvsfi8 (D19 pages, dark); this move is their in-Telegram container and auth.

moves.title: Place-keyed reminders: 'next time I'm at X' fires on OwnTracks region entry, with places named by dropping a Telegram pin
moves.why: Butlers already ingests OwnTracks region transitions (owntracks.py:116, :650-655) and movement episodes, but nothing owner-authored fires on them. Location is a Butlers-ahead area Dots cannot reach (gap_matrix_reach_actions.md:150, :371). Owner value is high: errands, gifts and returns happen at places, not times.
moves.payoff: The owner says 'when I'm next at Fairprice, get batteries and Sam's birthday card'. On region entry, one Telegram message arrives with the owner's own words and a Done button. The owner drops a pin with 'this is the climbing gym' and the place exists with no env edit. Expiring and once-only by default.
moves.integration_points: Table general.place_reminders (id, place_id, text owner-authored, once, expires_at, fired_at, lineage) plus an owner-editable named-place store public.owner_places (label, lat, lon, radius, source) replacing the OWNTRACKS_PLACE_REFERENCES env read (context_producers.py:630-653). A deterministic job matches owntracks transition envelopes and points against owner_places, then calls notify to the owner. Creating a reminder is a `record` with owner_authority from an owner-origin goal; it is NOT an `administer` obligation because no goal or LLM runs at fire time. telegram_bot.py:_extract_normalize…
moves.novelty: rg 'location.based reminder|location_reminder|place_trigger|when I (arrive|get to|leave)|arrival_trigger|geo.?trigger|place.?reminder' over src/, roster/, openspec/, about/ and docs/: 0. bd search location/arrive/presence: only retention (bu-s11n0s.7), presence gating (bu-8cdl1.11 closed) and the SSID editor (bu-x7x1r4). Ledger grep 'geofenc|arriv|location-aware': only run 11 #11, which is delivery-gating presence, not owner triggers.

moves.title: Departure sweep: on leaving home, one Telegram card listing what is open, unlocked or on, with one-tap fixes through RFC 0028
moves.why: Home MANIFESTO frames the home as cared for without another dashboard, and the actuation contract already classifies light/switch turn_off as reversible, cover close as consequential and lock as protected (roster/home/modules/actuation.py:25-42). Nobody checks the house when the owner leaves (butler-home spec only reacts to unexpected changes, spec.md:37-39). Dots has no home access at all.
moves.payoff: Five minutes after at_home clears, the owner gets: 'You left: garage door open, back door unlocked, living-room lights on. [Close garage] [Lock back door] [Lights off] [All fine]'. One tap per item; the actuation receipt (succeeded or unverified) edits the card in place.
moves.integration_points: A deterministic job in roster/home triggers on the at_home to away transition (context_producers.py:420-424). It reads ha_entity_snapshot against an owner-declared checklist (home.departure_checklist: entity_id, expected_state) and calls notify to the owner. Each fix button is a parked actuation in pending_actions whose tap is the existing signed approval callback (telegram_bot.py:1030-1075), executed through the home actuation module with home.ha_command_log receipts. lens-self-improvement.summary: Butlers already learns well from approvals: the autonomy tracker suggests standing rules, decision memory keeps approve/reject tallies, and the insight engine weights categories by engagement. QA and self-healing turn errors into PRs. What it lacks is any record of what it could not do. On RFC 0038, goal.complete and the D11 outcomes have no "unmet need" field. The session-close friction ledger (bu-8cdl1.9) has no goal-runtime successor, so it goes silent at the switch. The improvement-proposal spine (bu-8cdl1.15 and specify-improvement-proposal-spine) is specified but blocked. It predates RF…

findings.title: The goal runtime has no record of 'I could not do this'
findings.evidence: RFC 0038 D8 goal.complete only 'Record the goal outcome' (rfcs/0038:590); D11 outcomes completed|partial|failed (:645-650); goal-orchestration delta has no unmet/missing field (rg 'unmet|missing|no capability' specs/goal-orchestration/spec.md: none); bd search 'unmet' and 'capability request': no issues

findings.title: The improvement-proposal spine predates RFC 0038 and has no exposure or lineage

findings.detail: Goal invocations call through the broker, not as per-butler roles. A proposal born in an exposed goal (an injected email asking for 'a skill that forwards mail') would be indistinguishable from an owner-origin one.

findings.title: Approval edits destroy the drafted version and copy content into the audit log

findings.title: Learning from decisions stops at approvals
