findings.title: Telegram Approve executes a call the card never shows; the only dossier text comes from the model
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/notifications.py:106-123 (the card shows only Tool, Why, Blast radius, Reversibility, Expires, Review link) and :128-175 (it carries a signed approve callback token); gate.py:130-145 and :611-612 (_why, _blast_radius and _reversibility are model-supplied tool args); core/approval_callbacks.py has no risk or effect-class restriction; delivery_recovery.py:802 (the RFC 0023 path reuses the same card); about/heart-and-soul/security.md:186 'An approval executes the exact stored call the owner saw'
findings.detail: One tap can approve email_send_message to an outside address, connector_disconnect or a memory_entity_merge without the owner seeing the recipient or content. Under prompt injection, the attacker writes the 'Why'. bu-ys9hdx.1 is about to activate this card's delivery path, and the live E2E bu-24lu6.8.2 is still pending.

findings.title: Burst collapse leaves later approvals with no push at all
findings.evidence: notifications.py:199-205 (from the 4th park within 10 minutes, the first gets a digest and later ones are 'collapsed'); :177-196 (the digest is non-interactive, with a count taken at emission time); delivery_recovery.py:238 excludes collapsed actions from delivery; config.py:166 sets a 48h expiry, after which the action is denied
findings.detail: The relationship schema's daily 06:30 email_identity_enrichment can park up to 10 actions (relationship_jobs.py:3452; relationship/butler.toml:155-157). A calendar_respond or memory_reclassify parked in the next 10 minutes is never presented on its own and silently expires unless the owner opens the dashboard. RFC 0035 also excludes collapsed actions from reminders.

findings.title: Memory-hygiene proposals push through the same path as consequential approvals
findings.evidence: relationship_jobs.py:2766-2780 (memory_forget parked with approval_push_runtime), :3307 (memory_entity_merge), :3806 (relationship_assert_fact), :4154 (memory_reclassify); crons in relationship/butler.toml:128-157 (one daily, three weekly)
findings.detail: Internal curation with no outside recipient uses up the owner's burst budget and causes the collapse in the previous finding. It should be a reviewable set, not per-item pushes.

findings.title: The template-pinned exemption has no implementation substrate
findings.evidence: rules.py:41-73 (only exact, pattern via fnmatch, and any constraint types; no template type); capability-authorization delta spec.md:162-169 (requires 'owner-authored template whose slots accept only typed values'); bu-stbwjc's D4 field list has no content_params, so the broker cannot tell which args are content-bearing; rg for content_params/content-bearing in openspec and src finds nothing outside spec prose and HA
findings.detail: After the cutover, template-pinned rules are the only non-owner standing rules usable by exposed goals. As things stand, a 'template' rule can be decided only as an exact-value pin, and a pattern constraint on a body must be treated as free text.

findings.title: The template-pinned definition does not pin recipients, and identifier slots can leak data
findings.evidence: capability-authorization spec.md:162-169 and security.md:89-92 constrain only content-bearing args, and typed slots include 'identifiers'; RFC 0038 D4 under-exposure row exempts 'standing rules ... that are template-pinned' with no recipient condition
findings.detail: An injected exposed goal could send a fixed-template message to an address the attacker names, with an identifier slot carrying a phone number, account reference or entity id. Fixed text then still leaks data and spends the owner's voice.

findings.title: The promotion ladder will mint rules that cover almost nothing after the cutover
findings.evidence: autonomy_tracker.py:42-78 (the v2 fingerprint pins only safety-critical args, so a suggested communicate rule pins the recipient but not the content); autonomy-tracker delta spec.md:27-31 (exposed approvals don't count); bu-m1u7zy.1 choice A (no standing rule may approve a third-party-started goal's park-only effect); rules.py:191-199 (a 2026-07-05 audit found zero approval_rules rows)
findings.detail: A confirmed suggestion applies only to goals that never read outside content. Nothing tells the owner this, so a rule can look like it cuts taps when it will not.

findings.title: Absence Plans' headline example cannot run on RFC 0038
findings.evidence: bu-s11n0s.10 design: 'messenger telegram_reply to <partner> exact, max 20', merged into gate.py match_rules_from_list; bu-m1u7zy.1 choice A: park-only effects of third-party-started goals are never approved by a rule; RFC 0038 D13 lines on the exposure limit

lens-memory-knowledge.summary: Butlers already leads Dots on per-item memory control: confirm and retract per fact, retire and endorse per rule, knowledge gaps, server-stamped authority, and taint plus held candidates after the cutover. Its gaps are in moving knowledge between trust levels, and in provenance at the level of a whole answer and a whole source. Five problems are verified. (1) Owner endorsement exists only for rules, so a reported, web-derived or tainted fact can never become trusted, even though the cutover spec says tainted fact candidates are held "until the owner endorses it". (2) The owner's dashboard "Co…

findings.title: The lead's 'owner profile' has no defined source, store or edit surface
findings.evidence: RFC 0038 D15 :753-756 and architecture.md:389 name it; core-spawner delta spec.md:249,273 and butler-base-spec delta :375,382 put it in every lead system prompt; bu-kfnoah says LEAD.md is 'loaded into every lead with the owner profile' but builds only LEAD.md; `bd search "owner profile"` returns no issues; design.md and tasks.md never mention it
findings.detail: The highest-leverage steering text in the new runtime has no defined source of truth, no rule for what is admitted, no version and no owner-visible rendering. Without one, it will either be hand-written outside governance or quietly become a projection of whatever happens to be in Profile Facts.

findings.title: Facts cannot be endorsed; only rules can, though the cutover spec says tainted fact candidates wait for owner endorsement
findings.evidence: migrations/013_content_authority.py:46-47 add endorsed_at/endorsed_by to rules only; storage.py:3101 endorse_rule; api/routers/memory.py:1489 /rules/{id}/endorse has no fact counterpart; module-memory delta spec.md:28-30 ('held candidate ... until the owner endorses it') and :40-47 define endorsement for rules only
findings.detail: A third-party, web-derived or tainted fact stays 'reported by <sender>' or tainted forever. Knowledge-gap notices say 'Reported by <sender>, not verified' (docs/modules/memory.md:104-106), and the owner has no action that verifies them.

findings.title: Owner 'Confirm' on the dashboard runs the LLM's memory_confirm code: it resets decay, does not vouch and records no actor
findings.evidence: api/routers/memory.py:1075-1083 delegates to storage.confirm_memory; storage.py:2958-2961 runs only `UPDATE ... SET last_confirmed_at = now()`; FactDetailPage.tsx:97-111 shows Confirm as the commit pill
findings.detail: The owner thinks Confirm means 'this is true', but authority, credence and taint stay unchanged. Because an exposed session can make the same call through memory_confirm, a poisoned fact can be kept from fading, and the owner's confirmations cannot be told apart from the model's.

findings.title: A fact's link to its originating request is an optional argument the LLM supplies, not a server stamp
findings.evidence: modules/memory/__init__.py:1010-1018 (request_context described as 'Optional request context dict ... request_id (optional trace ID)'); tools/writing.py:273-288 reads it from the argument; facts.request_id in migrations/001_memory_schema.py:313; the module-memory delta spec.md:112-125 stamps authority and taint from the goal ledger, but not goal_id
findings.detail: Content authority is forge-proof, but 'which message, goal or research call did this come from' is not. That blocks citations, retraction scoped to a source, and any accounting of a poisoned source's reach.

findings.title: Taint is a single yes/no flag with no recorded cause, so containment cannot be scoped to one poisoned source
findings.evidence: capability-authorization delta spec.md:146-152 ('Domains SHALL taint records written under an exposed assertion'); module-memory delta spec.md:15-17; RFC 0038 :851-853 has approvals show 'whether it was exposed and to what', so the ledger knows the cause but memory rows do not
findings.detail: When the owner learns that a sender or web page was hostile, the only remedies are retracting facts one at a time or a full reset (the Dots model).

findings.title: Owner statements made inside an exposed goal are refused rather than parked, so they are lost
findings.evidence: RFC 0038 D4 table :307 (record under exposure: 'allowed and tainted, unless owner_authority, which is refused'); capability-authorization delta scenario 'Exposed sessions cannot write steering memory' (spec.md ~:183-185)
findings.detail: Example: 'research flights to Osaka, and remember I only fly window seats now.' The research exposes the goal, so the profile write is refused. Consolidation then puts the outcome episode in the tainted partition, and without fact endorsement the preference never reaches the profile.

findings.title: The goal ledger records effects but not what a goal read, so an answer cannot cite its sources
findings.evidence: RFC 0038 D17 :790-797 (ledger = admission, exposure, grants, effects, approvals, outcome); bu-0rbswe goal detail = delegation tree, effects, approvals, budget, outcome; context.search returns stamped items (RFC :592) that the broker already inspects for exposure
findings.detail: The data needed for 'why do you think that?' passes through the broker and is thrown away.

findings.title: Web research will expose most research-using goals, so the trusted share of memory shrinks unless there is a path back
findings.evidence: bu-6qaju2.4 Lineage bullet (broker marks the caller and goal exposed on every result); module-memory delta spec.md:191-193 (consolidation splits into untainted owner-class and all-other partitions); no fact endorsement (finding 2)
findings.detail: This is a projection from the specs: the more the owner uses research, the more outcome episodes and derived facts are tainted, and the more later goals are exposed by ordinary memory reads (more approvals for the owner).

findings.title: The owner cannot write or edit a fact's content from the dashboard; the only fact mutations are confirm and retract
findings.evidence: api/routers/memory.py route list: the only fact mutations are POST /facts/{id}/confirm (:1075) and /retract (:1157); study gap_matrix_runtime_control.md R18 caveat ('no create or edit of fact or rule content in the dashboard')

moves.title: Vouch: one owner-only verb that turns a reported, inferred, web-derived or tainted fact into an owner-attested one
moves.why: vision.md non-negotiable 1 (sovereignty) plus the gap between the cutover spec (module-memory delta :28-30, held until the owner endorses) and code that endorses rules only. Dots cannot do this at all: its memories cannot be inspected individually. Owner value: memory gets more trustworthy the more the owner uses it, instead of more tainted. Needs a one-line amendment to RFC 0038 D6 and REQ-module-memory-013: 'The owner MAY endorse a held, non-owner or tainted fact through an owner surface only; an endorsed fact reads as owner-class and untainted, keeps its original authority, taint and evide…
moves.payoff: A Telegram card reads: 'Sam said your passport expires 2027-03 (reported, not verified). [Vouch] [Retract] [Later]'. Vouch makes it a Profile Fact that no longer exposes later goals. A web-research fact ('Osaka JR pass now costs 50,000 yen', tainted) is vouched or dropped in one tap, and the owner's own statements made inside exposed goals stop being lost.
moves.integration_points: New memory migration: facts.endorsed_at, endorsed_by and pre-endorsement authority and taint kept. storage.endorse_fact mirrors endorse_rule (storage.py:3101), including compare-and-swap against retracted or superseded facts and the catalog upsert. POST /api/memory/facts/{id}/vouch beside /confirm (api/routers/memory.py:1075). GET /api/memory/facts?held=true for the review queue. Telegram callback buttons on the bu-24lu6.4 token helper and the bu-kqme7f.4 feedback substrate. The Profile Facts admission predicate becomes owner-class or endorsed, like RULE_ADMITTED_SQL at content_authority.py:4…
moves.novelty: `bd search endorse` found only bu-q7vx1q.23/.24 (rule batches). Ledger and open-beads greps for vouch, 'endorse fact' and 'fact endorse' returned nothing. bu-djjig (credence and owner_asserted precedence) sets the evidence class at write time and has no owner promotion verb. bu-ep4ks.14 slice 4 re-verifies fading facts but only resets decay. New: owner promotion of a fact's authority and taint, and parking owner statements made in exposed goals.

moves.title: Grounding receipts: the ledger records what each goal read, and every answer gets a 'Why?' button
moves.why: The doctrine of transparent memory (security.md, vision non-negotiable 1) extended from 'inspect any memory' to 'see which memories produced this answer'. Dots answers from a memory it cannot show. Owner value: the owner can check a surprising answer in seconds and correct the specific fact behind it.
moves.payoff: The owner taps 'Why?' under 'You're free Thursday; Sam's birthday dinner is Friday' and gets: 'calendar read 09:12; fact: Sam birthday 03-14 (you said, 2025-11); fact: dinner Friday (reported by Sam, email 03-02)', each linked to its detail page with Retract and Vouch. In reverse, a fact page shows 'used by 4 goals'.
moves.integration_points: Additive control-plane ledger table goal_reads (goal_id, invocation_id, domain, item_kind, item_id, stamp, taint, read_at; ids and stamps only, no content), written by the broker when it inspects stamped output for exposure (RFC 0038 D6, :445-451). Goal detail read model in bu-0rbswe. Fact detail 'used by' via GET /api/memory/facts/{id}/uses. Telegram 'Why?' button on bu-z0b0ah delivery. Effect class: read (no new capability). Region: control plane plus memory.
moves.novelty: `bd search sources` returned only degraded-envelope and education work. Greps of open-beads.tsv and pursuit-ledger.md for grounding, 'read receipt' and 'what .. read' returned nothing. bu-q7vx1q.26 adds a who-told-you line per fact (fact-level, not answer-level). bu-0rbswe goal detail has effects but no reads. New: per-goal read lineage and reverse usage.

moves.title: Distrust a source: contain a poisoned sender, web page or goal across all memory, reversibly
moves.why: Prompt injection from third-party content is the main threat (security.md, RFC 0038 D6), but D6 contains it only per session. Dots can only reset all memory. Owner value: when a phishing email or a hostile page is found, the owner closes everything it reached in one action without losing the rest. Needs no doctrine amendment, only a spec addition to module-memory: server-stamped lineage on every write.
moves.payoff: The owner opens a sender (or a research URL, or a goal) and taps 'Distrust'. Butlers shows: '11 facts and 1 rule derive from this source; 3 goals read them; 1 parked email draft quoted one.' Confirming holds all 12 items (excluded from recall, still inspectable), re-holds derived rules, and lists the affected goals and effects for review. 'Trust again' undoes it.
moves.integration_points: Module-memory delta: every episode, fact and rule write stamps goal_id and the exposure-cause references (inbound message id, sender entity, research call id from bu-6qaju2.4, connector record) from the verified assertion, replacing the LLM-supplied request_id (memory/__init__.py:1010-1018). New public.distrusted_sources table (kind, ref, by, at, reverted_at). The hold predicate joins it in recall, search, context and catalog reads. The cascade follows memory_links derived_from (001_memory_schema.py:338-357) and consolidation evidence (bu-27dxl.4.1). The reverse 'goals that read it' needs mov…
moves.novelty: `bd search cascade` found only catalog and edge cascades on single-fact retraction (bu-9ltqm, bu-lbmd3). `bd search poison` found an unrelated audit repair. Greps for distrust, quarantine and 'blast' in the ledger and open beads returned nothing; the one hit was ingest bearer-material quarantine (pursuit-ledger.md:303). New: retraction scoped to a source across memory, with server-stamped lineage.

moves.title: Define the owner profile: one compiled, versioned page that is exactly what every lead is told about the owner
moves.why: RFC 0038 D15 puts the owner profile in every lead's system prompt, but nothing defines it (finding 1). Making it a projection the owner can read and edit is what keeps 'inspectable memory' true for the most powerful steering text. Dots' memory is opaque. No amendment needed: this fills a gap D15 left open.
moves.payoff: /me shows 'What every Butlers lead is told about you', version 37: identity, household, standing preferences, communication style and hard nos, each line linked to its fact with Edit, Retract and Pin/Exclude. A change shows a diff and the new version. Each goal receipt cites the profile version it ran with, so 'it ignored my preference' becomes checkable.
moves.integration_points: A deterministic compiler (no LLM) in the memory domain that builds a byte-bounded profile from untainted owner-class or vouched facts whose predicate knowledge_class is identity or preference (bu-2jtfw.3 knowledge_class), plus owner pins and exclusions in a small owner_profile_overrides table. Versioned digest stored in a public.owner_profile_versions table. The runner reads the latest version at invocation start (core-spawner delta :249). Receipts record the digest (core-sessions delta :66 already names the profile as a provenance source). Dashboard page on the owner entity. Owner-authored e…
moves.novelty: `bd search "owner profile"` found nothing. `bd search profile` returned bu-2jtfw.3 (knowledge-classed Profile Facts pack for memory_context), bu-bagfg (receipt-feed cleanup) and bu-q7vx1q.27 (system producers allowlist). None defines the D15 owner profile, its versioning or its owner page. The frontend has no about-me or owner-profile page (rg of frontend/src).

moves.title: Learn the owner's voice from their edits to parked drafts, as owner-authored evidence the owner can see
moves.why: Preference learning from approvals with provenance (brief). RFC 0021 decision memory already tallies approve and reject per pattern (RFC 0021 §4 :161-180), but the richest signal, how the owner rewrites a draft, is discarded. Under RFC 0038 D13 the owner can edit a parked call before it runs. Dots learns style without telling you what it learned. No doctrine amendment.
moves.payoff: After the owner trims 'Best regards' and shortens three drafted replies, a candidate rule appears: 'Owner prefers sign-off "Cheers" and replies under 60 words to friends (from 3 edits: links)'. The owner endorses it once and later drafts follow it. Each edit stays inspectable as evidence.
moves.integration_points: The approvals executor's D13 edited-execution path (bu-cadcr1) writes, per edited approval, a structured edit record (capability, recipient class, field, word-level diff stats, owner-inserted spans) as an episode stamped owner and untainted, because the owner authored the edit. Consolidation in the owner partition derives candidate style rules with memory_links derived_from to each edit. Rules surface through the existing rule endorse route (memory.py:1489). Capability: none new; episode capture is deterministic daemon code (D18-compatible).
moves.novelty: `bd search edit` (40 results) found no draft-edit learning. RFC 0021 §4 records approve and reject tallies only. rg of approvals module for edited/owner_edited found nothing (editing a parked call arrives with D13). lens-comms-delegate (run 19) covers template-pinned replies, not learning from edits. New: owner edit diffs as owner-authored evidence for style rules.

lens-calendar-time.summary: Butlers already has a strong calendar base, including some things Dots lacks. It has CRUD, an overlap and back-to-back conflict scan, a read-only free-slot finder with no-meeting blocks, a precomputed per-attendee prep rail (notes, last met, open commitments), an end-of-day meeting debrief, and the insight broker's hold during focus and meeting context. The gaps are in what it does with that base. Prep is pull-only on the dashboard. The only phone prep is the 23:00 LLM digest, and its prompt asks for 'travel time' it has no data for. Location knowledge stops at a 'home in ~N min' ETA. The fre…

findings.title: The meeting prep rail never reaches the phone at meeting time
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py:1-56 (writes state key calendar/prep/<event_id>, read only by GET /api/calendar/workspace/prep/{event_id}); `rg -n -i 'notify|telegram|insight|push' calendar_prep.py` gives no hits; roster/relationship/butler.toml:86-90 runs it once a day at 06:52
findings.detail: The deterministic per-attendee envelope already exists (dunbar tier, notes, last_met, commitments). The only phone delivery is the night-before LLM digest (roster/general/butler.toml:37-62). A meeting added after 06:52 gets no prep envelope at all.

findings.title: The night-before prep prompt asks the model for travel time it has no data for
findings.evidence: roster/general/butler.toml:62 'Include prep notes (documents to review, travel time, items to bring)'; `rg leave.by|travel_time|distance.?matrix` over src/ and roster/ finds no travel-time source
findings.detail: The model can only guess or fabricate a figure. This conflicts with the 'evidence, not fabrication' principle in chronicler/adapters/owntracks_place_cluster.py:39-41.

findings.title: Location intelligence only knows the way home
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:600-720: run_commuting_eta_context_producer uses a linear closing speed toward the 'home' reference and publishes 'home in ~N min'
findings.detail: Chronicler already projects movement_episode (start/end lat-lon, chronicler/adapters/owntracks.py:582-589) and place_episode clusters, and calendar-completed episodes carry the event location (chronicler/adapters/calendar.py:452,590). Nothing joins them into place-to-place travel times or a leave-by estimate.

findings.title: The conflict scan cannot see a travel-infeasible back-to-back
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/calendar_workspace.py:1663-1681: a fixed back_to_back_gap_minutes=15 and overloaded_day_hours=6.0, checked for overlaps, density and overload only
findings.detail: Two meetings with a 15-minute gap 40 minutes of transit apart are not flagged. The write-time check in modules/calendar.py:3571-3691 is overlap-only too.

findings.title: The free-slot finder is not used by any roster prompt or skill
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:3438-3488 calendar_find_free_slots (read-only; honors no-meeting blocks and preferences); `rg -i 'free.?slot|find_free_slots' roster/` gives no hits
findings.detail: The scheduling engine exists, but no scheduling-negotiation flow (offer times, hold them, confirm) is built on it.

findings.title: Time is measured against 'usual', never against what the owner intends
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/dashboard-chronicles/spec.md:708-717 (Balance Rings vs usual baseline); src/butlers/chronicler/routines.py:1-40 (routine miner against history); `rg -i 'time budget|weekly target|time allocation|hours per week'` over src, roster, openspec/specs and about gives no hits
findings.detail: The day ribbon already shows planned intent against lived time (spec.md:694-706). There is no owner-declared target and no weekly review against one.

findings.title: Notification focus defense exists; time-critical alerts need the urgent path
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:1450-1500 (holds routine insights while a suppressing context signal is active); src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:162 URGENT_PRIORITY_THRESHOLD = 90; context_bus.py:21-35 has meeting, focused, commuting, sleeping and away signals
findings.detail: Focus-time defense for notifications is mostly built. A leave-now alert must use the urgent subcycle without overriding sleeping or away.

findings.title: Calendar invites and attendee updates remain ungated until bu-fg499t lands

Run 13 deferred a 'leave-by feed' as L-cost or amendment-gated (docs/redesigns/2026-09-03-jarvis-pursuit.md:211), because it assumed third-party routing egress. Learning from data Butlers already holds removes that blocker. Dots has no location history, so it cannot do this. No doctrine amendment is needed.

The conflict view flags: 'Thu 14:00 Tanjong Pagar then 14:15 one-north: you usually need 35 min; you will be about 20 min late.' The 23:00 digest uses real numbers instead of guessing travel time.

Rows come from at least 2 past completed calendar episodes (adapters/calendar.py:452,590) that overlap a place_episode, or from an owner pin. 3) A deterministic job, leave_by_producer, run…

What is new: travel times from history with zero egress, the event-to-place learner, and travel-infeasible conflicts.

moves.title: Find-a-time: offer slots with internal holds and an approval-parked owner-voice reply
moves.why: Dots is praised for scheduling help and drafting. Butlers has the slot engine (calendar.py:3438-3488) but no flow on top of it. Draft to sam@x: ...' with Approve, Edit and Discard. When Sam picks Wednesday, a parked 'create event with sam@x' approval appears and the other two holds release.

Holds are internal rows only, with no provider write, so free/busy shows nothing to others. New capabilities: calendar.hold_slots (effect class record, owner-only, owner_authority false) and calendar.release_holds (record). The reply uses bu-kqme7f.6 (reply in-thread as the owner, communicate, recipient_params) or the bot mailbox. The confirm step uses calendar_create_event with attendees (communicate, after…

Holding them against what the owner says they want turns the record into steering the owner chose (owner-authority record). Dots has no wearable, desktop or location evidence. No amendment is needed.

Thu 14:00-17:00 is free. Block it as focus?' Sunday: a 6-line review of target against actual, each line with an evidence link.

A deterministic weekly and midweek evaluator reads Activity-layer episodes (exercise, focus_block from adapters/focus.py, the who-you-were-with social lane) and forward calendar hours. It sends owner-notify insights. The optional focus block is a butler-calendar event with no attendees (calendar_create_event on the butler calendar, effect class record, owner origin, conflict policy sug…

Balance rings compare against 'usual' (dashboard-chronicles spec:708-717); the routine miner compares against history (routines.py). overloaded_day_hours is a query default, not an owner target (calendar_workspace.py:1672). open-beads grep 'focus|weekly review|time review': none on this topic.

moves.title: A protected work block for each owner promise with a deadline (deadline capacity check)
moves.why: Owner commitments already carry deadlines and escalation levels (calendar_prep.py:36-45), and escalation is time-only (commitment_escalation.py has no free/busy reads). Checking whether there is free time before the deadline turns 'you owe Sam the deck' into 'and you have 40 free minutes before Friday'. No amendment is needed.
moves.payoff: Tuesday: 'You promised Sam the deck by Fri. Your free time before then: Wed 16:00-16:40 only. Block Wed 16:00 and move Thu's optional 1:1? / Ask Sam for Monday (draft)?'
moves.integration_points: A deterministic check runs inside the commitment-escalation job (src/butlers/jobs/commitment_escalation.py). For owner_to_other commitments with a deadline, it calls the module's _find_free_slots over now to deadline and emits a capacity-at-risk insight when free time is below a default or owner-stated effort. Verbs: create a butler-calendar block (record, owner origin) or park a deadline-extension draft (communicate, park-only, recipient_params). RFC 0038: obligation origin with the default read plus owner notify grant; verbs run under owner origin after a tap.

lens-home-iot.summary: The run-11 lock hole is closed: lock.unlock, lock.lock and lock.open are protected (actuation.py:40-42), and _call_service parks them before any HA request (roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1745). The brief's premise is out of date: RFC 0038 already defines an `actuate` effect class (RFC 0038:288,310), so no "physical" class amendment is needed. The physical boundary now depends on what "reversible" means. That is decided per (domain, service) only, so an area, device or entity_id "all" target, or a critical smart plug (freezer, sump pump, router), runs with no approval. It also runs under exp…

findings.title: Run 11's ungated lock.unlock is fixed; locks, alarms and unknown services park before any HA request
findings.evidence: roster/home/modules/actuation.py:40-46 (lock.* and alarm_control_panel.* PROTECTED), :79-81 (unknown pairs default to PROTECTED); roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1745-1760 (requires_approval and no approval context → park and return pending_approval); bu-8cdl1.2 closed
findings.detail: Valve, siren, water_heater, media_player and similar unlisted services also fail closed as protected.

findings.title: 'Reversible' actuation is unbounded in target and payload: area, device or 'all' targets and critical switches run with no approval, including under exposure
findings.evidence: actuation.py:23-33 (risk keyed only on (domain, service)); :84-93 (non-entity targets return []); __init__.py:1720-1725 (data merged verbatim into the HA payload, so data={'entity_id':'all'} reaches HA); :1806-1811 (reversible needs only a rollback hint); RFC 0028:20 says reversible means 'a bounded action'; security.md:84-87 and RFC 0038:310 gate only consequential or protected actuation under exposure
findings.detail: switch.turn_off with target {'entity_id':'all'} or {'area_id':'kitchen'} executes before verification and settles 'unverified' afterwards. An email-exposed owner goal could cut power to a freezer or sump pump, and a smart plug on a fridge counts as 'reversible'.

findings.title: climate.set_temperature accepts any temperature and extra service fields, and its rollback cannot be executed
findings.evidence: actuation.py:33 (REVERSIBLE), :106-112 (rollback data is the placeholder string 'restore_previous_observed_temperature'); __init__.py:2166-2183 (_observe_target_states reads state only after the call, so no previous state is ever captured)
findings.detail: An hvac_mode or 35C payload passes as reversible, and the light/switch inverse ignores the prior state (turn_on on a light that was already on 'rolls back' to off).

findings.title: Life-safety events (leak, smoke, CO, gas) have no deterministic path: only an LLM skill on the frozen route handles them, and it does not list them
findings.evidence: roster/home/.agents/skills/ha-event-response/SKILL.md:30-50 (safety triggers name lock, cover and security binary_sensor only); __init__.py:1030-1067 (the module's WS handler only updates its cache); rg for moisture|smoke|carbon_monoxide|water_leak in src/roster (non-test) returns only home_assistant_pipeline.py:90 (a significance threshold)
findings.detail: Under the cutover, a device feed wakes reasoning only through a declared subscription (openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/connector-home-assistant/spec.md:5,14; RFC 0038:391-396). Until bu-o9qax4 declares one, a leak alert depends on a model goal.

findings.title: The insight broker cannot carry life-safety alerts: the urgent sub-cycle runs hourly and honours verbosity off
findings.evidence: about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0011-proactive-insight-delivery.md:332 ('30 * * * *', 'Verbosity off still applies'); :320 (notify priority high = 90 bypasses quiet hours and the context bus)
findings.detail: The brief suggests routing anomaly noticing 'through the insight broker'. For a leak or smoke alert that means up to 60 minutes of delay. Safety alerts need direct high-priority notify; the broker suits energy and maintenance insights.

findings.title: No signal tells the owner when home sensing goes offline
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/home.py:126-170 (_require_ha_source_healthy raises unmeasurable, and readers skip); rg ha_source_health finds only home module, router, context_producers, briefing, jobs/home; no owner_conditions or expected_signals producer for an HA outage
findings.detail: Failure no longer impersonates health in readers (bu-8cdl1.12 slice 1), but nothing tells the owner the house is blind while they are away.

findings.title: Presence has no confirmed-departure edge: away and unknown look the same on the context bus, and owner mapping is unconfigured
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:421-425 (away only clears at_home; unknown leaves the TTL to lapse); context_bus.py:85 (the 'away' signal is writable only by general); open beads bu-bdlr3 (configure home:presence:owner_entities) and bu-pvapy (owner HA person mappings)
findings.detail: Any departure or arrival routine needs a recorded transition from fresh home to fresh not_home, not an expired at_home TTL.

findings.title: The Home manifesto promises 'I'm leaving → lock doors, arm security', which the actuation contract forbids
findings.evidence: roster/home/MANIFESTO.md 'Device Orchestration' paragraph; openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/module-home-assistant/spec.md:10-12 ('No standing rule SHALL approve a consequential or protected call'); actuation.py:40-46
findings.detail: Today it is one approval tap per lock or alarm. The manifesto promise and the skill's 'execute corrective action silently' (ha-event-response SKILL.md:66) also exceed the RFC 0038 obligation default grant of read, record and owner notify (RFC 0038:382).

findings.title: There is no energy cost anywhere; home energy is kWh only
findings.evidence: rg -i 'tariff|cost|price|currency' in src/butlers/jobs/home.py returns only comments (:5, :1287); jobs/home.py:1551-1692 (kWh baselines from energy_baseline facts); Finance has a 'utilities' bill category (roster/finance/tests/test_upcoming_bills_skill_path.py:114)

moves.title: Bound reversible actuation: explicit entity targets only, a per-service data-key allowlist with comfort bounds, and owner-marked critical entities promoted to protected
moves.why: RFC 0028:20 defines reversible as 'a bounded action', and security.md:84-87 leaves reversible actuation open under exposure, so the boundary must hold in code; today any area, device or 'all' target, or a freezer plug, is one LLM call away. Owner value: the house cannot be mass-switched by a prompt-injected email.
moves.payoff: switch.turn_off {'entity_id':'all'}, any area_id, device_id, label_id or floor_id target, an unexpected data key, a set_temperature outside 16-30C, or a switch the owner marked 'critical' (fridge, sump pump, router) now parks for approval. Light, fan and thermostat nudges on named entities stay one-step.
moves.integration_points: roster/home/modules/actuation.py:79-93 (classify_actuation takes target and data; anything other than an explicit entity list within the per-service cardinality cap returns PROTECTED); __init__.py:1720-1745 (classify after the payload is built; reject entity_id inside data); new table home.entity_risk_overrides (entity_id PK, risk, reason, set_by, set_at), written only through a dashboard route as an `administer` effect with per-event approval; spec module-home-assistant 'Physical Actuation Risk Gate'; RFC 0038 D4: ha_call_service stays `actuate` with resource_params=['target'] and safety_arg…
moves.novelty: bd search 'actuation' finds only bu-8cdl1.2 (closed: the original gate). bd search 'risk' finds no home bead. The bu-svqpzo children (listed) cover calendar, insight origin and HA credential scrubbing (.11), not actuation scope. rg 'area_id|"all"' in actuation.py finds no guard. pursuit-ledger.md has only run 11 #2.

moves.title: Home safety sentinel: deterministic leak/smoke/CO/freezer/open-door detection with a standing condition, an immediate owner alert, a one-tap parked mitigation and an honest 'house is blind' signal
moves.why: Home MANIFESTO 'alerting you to problems before they become serious' and vision 'failure never impersonates health'. Today a leak reaches the owner only if an LLM on the frozen route classifies it, and the post-cutover feed path wakes nothing without a declared subscription. Dots cannot see the house at all.
moves.payoff: Within seconds, and with no model in the loop: 'Kitchen leak sensor wet since 14:02. You are in Tokyo (trip active). [Close main water valve] [Snooze 30m]'. It re-escalates while the leak stays wet and closes itself when dry. When HA has been unreachable for 30 minutes while the owner is away: 'Home sensing offline since 13:10; leaks and doors are not being watched.'
moves.integration_points: Edge hook in roster/home/modules/__init__.py:1030-1067 (_handle_ws_event, after the cache update) plus a 5-minute reconcile job over ha_entity_snapshot gated by _require_ha_source_healthy (jobs/home.py:126). The owner declares roles in new table home.safety_watch (entity_id, role leak|smoke|co|gas|freezer_temp|door_open_away, threshold, mitigation_call jsonb). State goes to public.owner_conditions via reconcile_snapshot (src/butlers/core/owner_conditions.py), source 'home:safety' / 'home:sensing-blind'. Delivery is notify priority high (RFC 0011:320), never the broker. The mitigation is a par…
moves.novelty: Ledger: run 11 #12 (bu-8cdl1.12) S4 'anomaly baselines' is statistical drift; this is rule-based life safety with a condition ledger and is not filed. ha-event-response SKILL.md is LLM-driven on the frozen path. rg moisture|smoke|carbon_monoxide in src/roster finds no detector. bd search 'garage' finds nothing; 'leak' hits only log-handler beads. open-beads grep for leak|safety returns no home bead.

moves.title: Departure sweep: on a confirmed leave, one Telegram message lists what was left open, with a tap to fix each item
moves.why: The Home manifesto promises 'Say I'm leaving and we handle it', but locks and alarms are protected and no standing rule may approve them. The governed version checks automatically and lets the owner fix each item with one tap. Dots has no presence or home state.
moves.payoff: Six minutes after the owner leaves: 'Garage OPEN, study AC on, back door unlocked. [Close garage] [AC off] [Lock back door]'. Each tap runs one receipted call, and the reply confirms the verified state ('Garage closed, verified 18:07'). If nothing is open, nothing is sent.

The owner declares a leave-check list in home.leave_checks (entity_id, expected_state, fix_call jsonb). The message goes out through notify, with buttons as parked actions decided through signed Telegram callbacks (RFC 0021). moves.title: Owner-signed homecoming routine: pinned reversible pre-conditioning triggered by ETA or flight landing
moves.why: Home MANIFESTO 'When you walk into a room, it's already adjusted to your liking'. Only Butlers sees the flight status, OwnTracks ETA and home together; HA automations cannot see the flight, and Dots cannot see the home. Atmosphere pre-conditioning is advisory only today.

Creation is an `administer` effect with per-event approval. Triggers: the commuting ETA (context_producers.py:43-53) and flight_status 'landed' (jobs/flight_status.py:114-129). Execution is deterministic and calls the module handler only when the pinned call classifies reversible under move 1, HA is healthy and at_home is false, under receipt actor 'routine:<id>'. Undo uses the rollback hint. RFC 0038: an obligation created by `administer` whose capability set is…

moves.why: Under RFC 0038 the monthly ceiling disappears with the spawner (spawner.py:2172-2215), and today's version is fail-open and halts owner turns too. D10 requires every budget check to fail closed, and the vision promises an owner who steers cost without reading logs. Owner value H: always-on background work can never starve the owner's own requests, and no lane can quietly take 85% of the bill again (bu-h40h2b.9).

Background lanes stop at (1-r) of the ceiling and owner goals keep r (default 20%). Example: with a $100 ceiling, background stops at $80 and the owner keeps $20, about 250 owner goals at the Sol rate of $0.079. /status on Telegram shows 'obligation lane 78% of $40, owner reserve intact', and an 80% crossing sends one owner notify.

moves.title: Obligation preconditions: a deterministic 'anything to judge?' gate before a lead is admitted
moves.why: about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md:300-312 makes connectors the cost boundary, but obligations (schedules, subscriptions, watches) have no equivalent, and bu-o9qax4's declaration format names only a capability set. RFC 0038 D16 already says 'code gathers the state; the model only judges'. Owner value M-H: fewer empty runs and fewer 'nothing to report' pings, and more standing watches fit under the same cap.
moves.payoff: Each obligation declares precondition = non_empty(<domain read>) | changed_since_last(<domain read>) | window(<time query>), plus max_skips (forced run every N). A skipped occurrence records 'skipped_precondition' and costs no model. Example: an owner 'watch this page hourly' is 24 admissions a day, about 1 a day once gated, so about 22 × $0.079 ≈ $52 a month saved per hourly watch at the Sol rate. upcoming-travel-check skips on days with no trip in range.
moves.integration_points: Declaration block in roster/*/butler.toml and runtime obligations (bu-o9qax4 format decision). The domain's dark obligation submitter evaluates the precondition through deterministic domain read code (not model-reachable) before calling admission (bu-fkoexp). The digest is stored on the obligation occurrence row. Spec delta to core-scheduler and domain-event-bus. Effect class: none at evaluation; creating or changing a precondition on a runtime obligation is administer, parked. Generalizes the ad hoc job-then-admit pattern of the cross-source monitor (bu-kqme7f.3 seeds watermark).

moves.title: Cache-stable lead prefix contract with a cached-share deadman per role
moves.why: architecture.md:217-228 asks Butlers to measure cache behavior, and pricing.toml prices cache reads at 0.05x (Opus 5.5) to 0.1x (Sol, Luna). deep-design-2.summary: Owner Projects can be built inside RFC 0038 without reopening the settled approval rule. Approving it follows D13 (the approved digest is what runs) through the apr1 tap or a dashboard submit click, which the owner accepted as an approval in bu-4m4e42 item 1. It approves no future effec…

findings.title: A responsibility journal kept in task_continuity exposes every later run
findings.evidence: openspec/changes/generalist-lead-focused-delegation/specs/core-scheduler/spec.md:151-155 ('A tainted live row SHALL make the occurrence's goal start exposed'); harvest coverage-runtime move 'Owner-delegated responsibilities' integration_points (progress reuses public.task_continuity via carry_forward)
findings.detail: After the first check-in that reads mail writes progress, every later occurrence starts exposed. A single overwritten blob also loses history. Project check-ins must set continuity=false and keep their journal in a separate store that is read only when needed.

findings.title: Under D6, almost any read exposes a check-in, not just tainted reads
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:431-432 (stamped output exposes when any item 'is not owner authority' or carries taint); src/butlers/modules/memory/content_authority.py:10-16 (scheduled/internal writes stamp 'system', not owner-class)
findings.detail: An untainted log entry written by a check-in is stamped 'system' and still exposes its reader, and calendar and mail reads are third-party-writable. A useful check-in should be assumed exposed. What exposure costs is cached-only research (bu-6qaju2.4 line 5), inert links (D4), refused owner_authority writes, and parked communicate. The design has to make each of these cheap.

findings.title: An obligation check-in cannot even park an administer effect
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:311 (administer: per-event approval, never delegable); :383 (obligation default grant: read, record, owner notify); core-scheduler delta :34 (schedule_* catalogued administer outright)
findings.detail: lens-long-goals proposed `project.request_wake` as a parked administer effect from an obligation goal, but that goal holds no administer. An extra wake must therefore be a `record` proposal that the owner turns into an obligation through an owner-decision tap.

findings.title: One approval of an enumerated bundle is RFC-native, not a standing rule
findings.evidence: RFC 0038 D13:698-712 (park with exact args; on approval execute the stored call; 'the executed digest is the digest the owner approved'); bu-4m4e42 notes item 1 ('a dashboard submit click is the recorded owner approval'); core-scheduler delta :34 (one prompt-mode schedule_create already creates a recurring obligation from one administer effect)
findings.detail: An approved recurring schedule_create already arms many future occurrences with one tap, and project.arm is the same act over a pinned list. Standing rules (D13:713-718) auto-approve future effects that match; arming approves no effect.

Vendor doors:
- They need the deep-design-1 amendment to the D4 communicate row and REQ-006, not only the security.md line.
- 'Tainted records can fill a placeholder' opens an exfiltration channel. A path or query slot can carry goal data to the vendor host on tap. Slots must be typed and bounded (an order id pattern, for example), or there should be none.

findings.title: Homecoming routine lets tainted, email-derived rows trigger actuation without declaring an RFC 0038 amendment
findings.evidence: home-iot move 4 integration_points: trigger flight_status 'landed' (jobs/flight_status.py:114-129), runs pinned reversible calls deterministically. Its assurance admits 'a forged email-derived trip could at worst fire a bounded, reversible ... AC change'. RFC 0038:384: third_party never gets actuate. D6 taint.
findings.detail: The move declares only an RFC 0028 amendment. A deterministic trigger keyed on tainted rows launders third-party input into actuate, the effect class D5 denies to third-party origin. It needs a declared D5/D6 amendment, or a trigger limited to untainted sources (owner ETA only, or a flight leg the owner confirmed).

findings.detail:
Mini App:

- Validating initData puts the bot token in the dashboard API, which widens its custody beyond Messenger.

Outside-MCP adapter:
- Pinning schema digests does not pin upstream behaviour.
- Every call discloses its arguments to the vendor. It should be classed as disclosure to a third party, not plain read.

deep-design-3.summary:
Four lenses' presence and time features share one missing substrate, and most of it is cheap. Deterministic jobs come through the RFC 0038 cutover unchanged (RFC 0038:221-222), so the substrate can ship now as service-plane jobs and owner routes. None of it needs the frozen classify-and-route path or a subscription obligation, and a life-safety alert never depends on admitting a goal.

The substrate has three pieces:
- **One place registry the owner edits.** Today places live in three stores with no trusted editor: an operator env var, the SSID state key behind bu-x7x1r4, and the owner-entiti…

findings.title: No minute-resolution timed delivery lane; the only deliver_at is a quiet-hours hold, and held rows can arrive up to 24h late
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/butler.toml:86-95 (daily cycle 15,45 6-11; urgent '30 * * * *'); broker.py:1547-1610 (_compute_catchup_deliver_at is the only deliver_at); rg 'not_before|deliver_after|fire_at' broker.py = 0; scheduler.py:1920-1937 (deferred rows expire only >24h past deliver_at, delivered without re-gating per RFC 0011 'Notify-Path Holds'); config.py:231 tick_interval_seconds=60
findings.detail: A 'leave by 08:40' or 'you left the door unlocked' observation either waits up to 60 min in the broker or, as a held direct notify, lands after quiet hours as stale noise. The 60s scheduler tick means a timed lane is cheap to add.

findings.title: Presence has no persisted edge: 'away' is only a signal clear on a 10-minute cadence, and nothing consumes it
findings.evidence: context_producers.py:420-425 (False clears at_home/in_space; None leaves the TTL); :202 _PRESENCE_FRESHNESS 30m; :207 _AT_HOME_REFRESH_TTL 25m; roster/home/butler.toml:93-97 cron */10; context_bus.py:85 'away' writable only by general
findings.detail: A departure is visible only as at_home disappearing, up to 10 min late. Nothing records when the owner left or from which source, and nothing distinguishes a retracted departure from a real one.

findings.title: OwnTracks region transitions are not persisted for deterministic consumers
findings.evidence: connectors/owntracks.py:1386-1392 (transition becomes an ingest envelope to Switchboard only); :1445 persist_location_point runs only for payload_type=='location'
findings.detail: The fastest departure signal (a phone-side region 'leave') reaches only the frozen classify path today. After cutover it wakes nothing, so deterministic edge fusion cannot use it.

findings.title: Place definitions are split across three stores, and none has a trusted owner editor
findings.evidence: context_producers.py:641 and owntracks_place_cluster.py:45,162 (env OWNTRACKS_PLACE_REFERENCES); chronicler/adapters/owntracks_ssid.py:66 (state key chronicler/owntracks/ssid_places, editor bu-x7x1r4 blocked); context_producers.py:198 (home:presence:owner_entities, route bu-bdlr3 blocked; mapping bu-pvapy open)
findings.detail: The owner cannot add 'gym' or 'mum's place' at all. Coordinates are operator env config, and a place-keyed feature would need a fourth store.

findings.title: A Telegram location pin loses its coordinates at ingest
findings.evidence: connectors/telegram_bot.py:152 ('location': 'Location'), :212 returns '[Location]' (only poll, sticker and contact are enriched)
findings.detail: The natural phone gesture for 'save this place' reaches Butlers as the bare text '[Location]'.

findings.title: Insight candidates can carry only one prepared-action door, and only relationship has a status resolver
findings.evidence: broker.py:1061-1063 (_PREPARED_ACTION_STATUS_QUERIES = {relationship}); broker.py:1066-1136 render_prepared_action_door per candidate
findings.detail: A departure card with three one-tap fixes needs a home resolver and several doors per candidate.

findings.title: Parked HA actuations expire after a fixed 24h and push their own approval message
findings.evidence: roster/home/modules/__init__.py:2050-2087 (expires_at=now+24h, session_id nullable); modules/approvals/park.py:548-595 (rollout-gated admission and outbox; deduplication_key supported)
findings.detail: Without a card-embedded park mode, a sweep with three fixes would produce three separate approval pushes, and a 'lock door' fix would stay approvable after the owner is home again.

findings.title: Deterministic jobs come through the cutover unchanged, so this substrate is off the frozen path
findings.evidence: RFC 0038:216-222 (D2 'Deterministic jobs and reactions (sweeps, syncs, projections) are unchanged'); RFC 0038:391-396 (feeds wake reasoning only through declared subscriptions); RFC 0038:799-828 (D18 covers model use only)
findings.detail: Presence producers, the departure sweep and leave-by need no goal admission or bu-o9qax4 subscription, as long as they never wake a model.

findings.title: Calendar event location is free, third-party-authorable text
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_003_calendar.py:73 (location TEXT); RFC 0038:391-396 (fields a non-owner can author are untrusted)
findings.detail: A leave-by join must treat the location only as an exact-match key and render it inert. It must never be a geocoding query or prompt input.

moves.title: Owner places and confirmed presence edges: one owner-edited place registry, a fused leave/enter edge log, and coordinate-free travel legs
moves.why: Vision asks Butlers to notice useful work before the owner asks (vision.md:7) and to keep failure from impersonating health. The Home manifesto promises 'Say "I'm leaving" and we handle it' (roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:17). Today places are operator env config, departure is an unrecorded signal clear (context_producers.py:420-425), and leave-by history dies with raw fixes (bu-s11n0s.7). Dots has no location at all. No doctrine amendment is needed: everything stays inside the location retention promise (security.md:337-339).
moves.payoff: The owner names places from the dashboard (and later from a Telegram pin): 'Gym, 150 m'. Chronicles shows 'Left home 08:12 (HA + GPS), arrived Office 08:47', and every presence or time feature (sweep, leave-by, place reminders, the sentinel's away mode) reads one confirmed edge instead of re-deriving presence.

moves.title: Timed and immediate delivery lanes, with the departure sweep as first consumer: one card when the owner leaves, each open item fixable by one tap
moves.why: Time- and presence-anchored observations are worthless an hour late, but RFC 0011's broker delivers urgent items hourly (RFC 0011:332) and holds expire after 24h (scheduler.py:1920-1937). The Home manifesto promises 'Say "I'm leaving" and we handle it' and 'alerting you to problems before they become serious' (MANIFESTO.md:17, :35). The governed version is check, report, and one-tap fix: locks and covers stay protected or consequential under the RFC 0028 risk map (actuation.py:25-48). Dots cannot see the house. This needs an RFC 0011 amendment (not heart-and-soul doctrine): 'A timed candidate…

Can't see: back door sensor (unavailable).' A tap executes that exact receipted call. Arriving home cancels any untapped fixes. If everything is secure, nothing is sent unless the owner opts into 'All secure'.

moves.title: Leave-by nudges learned from the owner's own trips: calendar event to place to p80 travel time, delivered on the timed lane, with no geocoding or routing egress
moves.why: Vision asks for timely, relevant insights without being asked (vision.md:182). Run 13 deferred a leave-by feed because it assumed routing-API egress (docs/redesigns/2026-09-03-jarvis-pursuit.md:211). Learning from the owner's own travel_legs removes the egress, and v1.md:52 forbids no derivation over held data. Dots has no location history, and phone OS assistants send location to a vendor. No doctrine amendment is needed.
moves.payoff: At 08:30 the owner gets: 'Leave by 08:40 for Dentist (Novena): usually 32 min from Office (p80 of 7 trips).' Buttons: [Snooze 5] [Not going] [Not now / Never]. If the owner has already left Office, nothing is sent. Unmatched events show 'no estimate: tell me where this is' on the dashboard prep view instead of a guessed time.
